#2260. Napoli-Lazio 1-1, le pagelle di IamNaples.it: Lang il migliore, bene Olivera

Ecco le pagelle di IamNaples.it  dell’1-1 tra il Napoli e Lazio:

Milinkovic-Savic 6,5: Riesce a salvare il risultato nel primo tempo, soprattutto sul colpo di testa di Sutalo.

Beukema 5,5: Soffre tantissimo nella prima frazione, migliora un poco nella ripresa ma è sempre impreciso.

Rrahmani 5,5: Esprime ancora tante difficoltà, anche se mostra qualche miglioramento rispetto alla gara contro il Porto.

Rafa Marin 6: Ancora il migliore della difesa.

Vergara 5,5: Non ne prende una, soffre perennemente. Meglio nella ripresa. Dal 74’ Politano S.V.

De Bruyne 6: Non sempre preciso quest’oggi, da segnalare più di qualche corsa all’indietro.  Si mangia il gol del 2-1. Dall’83’ Giovane 5,5: Entra per pochi minuti, ma riesce comunque a rendersi pericoloso.

Gilmour 5,5: Non riesce a rendere compatta la squadra,  realizza un paio di coperture molto importanti. Dal 69’ Anguissa 6: Dà ordine al centrocampo.

McTominay 5,5: Primo tempo inesistente, uno dei peggiori. Mentre nella ripresa riesce a dare la scossa.

Olivera 6: Recuperato e messo subito in campo ed è uno dei migliori.

Lang 6,5: Al netto della diatriba con le curve e di qualche imprecisione, vuoi o non vuoi, è il migliore del Napoli

Hojlund 5,5: Solita gran lotta, ma oggi sicuramente un passo indietro rispetto alle sue consuete gare. Dal 74’ Lucca 5: Ci mette un po’ più d’anima, ma tanta confusione.

#2258. Lazio-Lecce, biglietti in vendita dal 9 novembre: orari e modalità

La gara è in programma sabato 21 novembre alle 15:00; per gli acquisti online è prevista una commissione del 3,80%.

I biglietti per Lazio-Lecce saranno in vendita dalle 11:00 di lunedì 9 novembre. La partita di Serie A Enilive è in programma sabato 21 novembre alle 15:00. Secondo quanto riportato da Sslazio, La S.S. Lazio ha comunicato le modalità di acquisto, le agevolazioni e le indicazioni per l’accesso allo Stadio Olimpico.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Le tariffe per invalidi al 100% e persone in carrozzella, entrambe previste con accompagnatore, sono acquistabili soltanto nei negozi Lazio Style 1900, escluso quello di Parco Leonardo. La stessa indicazione riguarda i biglietti ridotti per invalidi civili al 100% e per la Tribuna Tevere non deambulanti, in entrambi i casi con accompagnatore.

Chi possiede una fidelity card Millenovecento o Eagle e non è abbonato può chiedere, anche acquistando online, che il titolo d’ingresso venga caricato elettronicamente sulla carta. Ai biglietti comprati online si applica una commissione di servizio del 3,80%.

Nella vendita libera una persona può acquistare al massimo quattro biglietti, secondo le disposizioni dell’Osservatorio sulle Manifestazioni Sportive. Per gli altri tre eventuali spettatori è sufficiente presentare anche una copia del documento d’identità.

Il biglietto Ridotto Under 16 è riservato ai ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2010. Per i nati dal 1° gennaio 2012 è prevista l’iniziativa Omaggio Under 14: possono entrare gratuitamente se accompagnati da un genitore, o da un parente entro il quarto grado, titolare di un biglietto a pagamento.

Il tagliando omaggio, nominativo, va ritirato insieme all’acquisto del biglietto dell’accompagnatore. L’operazione si svolge esclusivamente nei Lazio Style 1900, tranne Parco Leonardo, oppure, solo il giorno della gara, alla biglietteria di Via Nigra. La comunicazione del club rimanda alle indicazioni dedicate agli omaggi Under 14.

I bambini nati dal 1° gennaio 2022, indicati nella comunicazione come bambini di quattro anni, entrano gratuitamente senza biglietto presentando un documento d’identità o la tessera sanitaria. All’ingresso l’identità sarà controllata per ogni spettatore: anche i minorenni devono esibire un documento.

#2257. Celtic ‘don’t have the legs’ as Chris Sutton unearths January transfer priority

Chris Sutton believes Celtic “don’t have the legs in midfield” to play Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran together.

The former striker has questioned whether Martin O’Neill can find room for both centre-forwards in his current system, despite wanting to see the partnership given an opportunity.

Hogh endured another frustrating evening in the 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas, while Duran came off the bench and struck twice to complete the comeback.

Sutton feels Hogh has suffered from a lack of service and believes the Dane could benefit from operating alongside Duran. Writing in his Daily Record column, Sutton said: “He’s struggling for decent service and I’d still like to see O’Neill finding a way to get him and Duran on the pitch at the same time.

The Celtic star who is 'absolute saviour' and teammate full of 'magic'

Celtic told ‘we’ll fight to win’ as Portuguese minnows dare to dream

Mika Baur gets Germany call-up after Celtic star misses senior cut

“We know why it can’t happen though, Celtic don’t have the legs in midfield to cope so it might be something that has to wait until that is addressed in the January transfer window.”

Sutton believes there can be little doubt over who should lead the line for Celtic. He added: “In the meantime Duran simply has to start. You could say the same about Osmand.”

Duran’s double against Besiktas strengthened his case for a regular central role, while Callum Osmand also made a major impact from the bench with a goal and an assist.

#2256. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Gabriel misses his penalty ❌PSG WIN THE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE!!! 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/6XSuU3xqsN

Mattéo Guendouzi, the former Arsenal fireband, was at the heart of chaotic and ugly scenes in the Champions League qualifying play-off between Lyon and his side Fenerbahce, culminating in a brawl at the mouth of the tunnel.

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Matteo Guendouzi has not forgotten who his rivals are... 👀The former Marseille player made his feelings known as Fenerbahce knocked out Marseille's rivals Lyon. pic.twitter.com/pjDKPqPzZD

As he gestured towards the fans, while being shepherded by team-mates, objects were thrown from the crowd. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

AEK, LASK, Viking, Slovan Bratislava, Sabah Baku, Fenerbahce and Bodo/Glimt were the seven teams to come through the play-offs.

Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. #2255. Barcellona, Lamine Yamal diventa il re degli assist in Europa: sale a 12 e supera Kane

Il Barcellona si gode un Lamine Yamal sempre più determinante. Anche nella vittoria per 2-1 contro l'Atletico Madrid, il talento classe 2007 ha lasciato il segno, fornendo a Fermín López l'assist che ha avviato la rimonta blaugrana. Un passaggio vincente che gli ha permesso di raggiungere quota 12 assist stagionali, diventando il miglior assistman tra i giocatori dei cinque principali campionati europei. Otto sono arrivati nella Liga e quattro in Champions League. Alle sue spalle figurano Harry Kane, fermo a 11, e il terzetto composto da Florian Thauvin, Nico Paz e Marco Grüll, tutti a quota otto.

La prestazione del diciannovenne al Metropolitano non si è limitata all'assist. Yamal è stato il giocatore più intraprendente della partita, completando sei dribbling e creando sette occasioni da gol. Ha inoltre effettuato tre cross, completato 13 passaggi nella trequarti avversaria e vinto due contrasti, confermando una partecipazione sempre più completa alle due fasi di gioco.

Con 13 gol e 12 assist complessivi, l'esterno spagnolo è già sulla strada per superare i propri migliori numeri personali. A 19 anni è diventato uno dei principali riferimenti tecnici della squadra di Hansi Flick, assumendo responsabilità crescenti anche sul piano della leadership. Un'evoluzione testimoniata dal suo ingresso tra i capitani del Barcellona.

#2254. Allegri a DAZN: “Gara importante, voglio ringraziare i ragazzi. La squadra si è compattata”

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, è intervenuto ai microfoni di DAZN dopo il pari contro la Lazio: “Voglio ringraziare i ragazzi che hanno disputato una gara importante. Non era semplice dopo le sconfitte contro Porto e Torino. Abbiamo avuto delle situazioni favorevoli anche nel primo tempo, ma nel secondo è stata tutta un’altra storia. Abbiamo avuto 8 gare nello stesso mese. Il fatto che la squadra si sia compattata è stato un piccolo mattoncino. La squadra ha disputato un bel secondo tempo. Da sinistra crossavamo. Invertendo i colpitori, McTominay ci sarebbe stato più utile. Nel primo tempo i cross arrivavano i cross, Vergara era ben coperto, quindi ho dovuto invertire. Dobbiamo continuare a lavorare con fiducia. Abbiamo perso molti punti, ma non siamo troppo lontani dalla zona Europa. Dobbiamo lavorare seriamente e migliorare ciò che manca semplificando le cose. Critiche a Lang? Si sa, i tifosi criticano quando va male. Ci sostengono sempre. Con ordine riusciremo ad uscirne. Come sto? Sto assolutamente bene. Fortunatamente di questi periodi ne ho passati pochi, ma quando siamo in mezzo alla tempesta, la barca va portata nel porto. Lo stiamo facendo nel migliore dei modi, dobbiamo sostenere i ragazzi”.

#2253. Martin O’Neill answers Celtic ‘chucked it’ claims after major team gamble

Chris Sutton has praised Martin O’Neill for making his critics “eat their words” after Celtic breathed new life into their Europa League campaign.

There was widespread surprise when O’Neill named a much-changed side to face Besiktas, with Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand among those left on the bench.

Writing in his Daily Record column, Sutton admitted he shared some of those concerns but held fire on criticising the Celtic boss. He said: “Martin O’Neill has chucked it. The Celtic team sheet is more like a white flag. He’s given up the ghost in Europe.

Celtic injury update as key star battles hamstring issue

The ongoing Celtic problem that must be ‘addressed’ in January

Chris Sutton delivers brutal ‘all-inclusive holiday’ jibe at new Celtic star

“Those were just some of the messages that lit up my phone when the team was announced for Besiktas the other night.

"I might have had similar feelings but I didn’t respond because I know football has a funny habit of biting you on the backside. And Martin O’Neill has a funny way of making folk eat their words.

“Turns out I was right to withhold judgement.”

#2251. Italia senza Cristante, Bernardeschi e Calò? Mancini spiega: "Ora abbiamo bisogno di altre soluzioni"

Questa è la Nazionale di Mancini con l'età media più bassa: merito anche di questo campionato? Nella prima conferenza stampa da Coverciano che inaugura la sosta per le nazionali e che vedrà protagonista anche l'Italia in Nations League, il ct Roberto Mancini risponde anche a questa domanda: "Non mi sembra che la situazione sia cambiata, è grossomodo la stessa. C'è qualcuno che li fa giocare, altri no. Ma noi abbiamo l'obbligo di cercarli e di convocare ragazzi giovani per conoscerli direttamente. Per questo motivo chiamiamo anche ragazzi giovani con buone qualità tecniche. Pensiamo che nel giro di non molto tempo possano diventare bravi".

Nazionale di ringiovanimento o di ricambio generazionale? Perché non ci sono Cristante, Bernardeschi e Calò? "Bernardeschi e Cristante li conosciamo, non c'è bisogno di provarli. Quando avremo bisogno di loro li chiameremo. Ora abbiamo bisogno di altre soluzioni, giocatori più giovani che devono fare esperienza. Calò è uno dei tanti ragazzi che stanno facendo bene in questo momento, il Frosinone ne ha 3-4 bravi. Ma non possiamo chiamare giocatori di 29-30 anni in questa fase, quando servirà lo faremo ma non perché ce lo dice il suo procuratore". Il riferimento, appunto, è alle parole dell'agente del centrocampista rilasciate in esclusiva a TMW.

Sui giovani che ha portato cosa ci dice di più? "Lontani mi ha destato una buona impressione già dalla prima di campionato, poi è migliorato gara dopo gara. Ha personalità e qualità tecniche. Cassano può essere il giocatore che noi non abbiamo in questo momento, è un ragazzino ma è un regista di centrocampo che ha il gioco in testa e gioca in una squadra dove giocano a calcio e pensano allo stesso modo. Gli altri sono già un po' più grandi e già si conoscevano".

#2250. Dundee United 1-1 Motherwell: Backheel beauty earns hosts a point

Dundee United and Motherwell had to be content with a share of the spoils in a 1-1 draw after an entertaining Premiership contest at Tannadice.

Steelmen skipper Lukas Fadinger gave his side the lead from the penalty spot, with Jesse Randall equalising for the home side before the break with a moment of magic.

Neither side could find a winner in the second half but United have now extended their unbeaten run to seven games to remain sixth in the table while Motherwell stay ninth.

The Steelmen took the lead in the ninth minute. Tawanda Maswanhise tumbled in the home box under a challenge from Dylan Tait but the linesman’s flag went up for offside.

However, referee Ryan Lee was called over to the pitchside monitor by the VAR Andrew Dallas and decided to award a penalty. Fadinger stepped up and sent United goalkeeper Jack Walton the wrong way.

Shortly after, United were claiming for a penalty of their own when Zac Sapsford went down in a challenge with Emmanuel Longelo but the whistler flashed a yellow card at the Terrors striker for diving.

Maswanhise then created an opening of his own, embarking on a barnstorming run but his shot flew straight to Walton, who easily gathered.

Motherwell’s Ibrahim Said was next to try his luck from 22 yards but again his effort was straight at Walton and then Sapsford hit a snap-shot that was well saved by the visitors’ goalie Alexander Paulsen.

Walton was called into action again in the 28th minute when Tom Sparrow found Longelo inside the United box with the defender hitting a shot into the ground that the keeper had to acrobatically tip over, before Daniel Bennie went close at the other end with a header.

Paulsen then made two smart saves in quick succession from shots by Lyall Cameron and then Tait.

However, the keeper could not prevent United equalising in the 41st minute when the ball found its way to Randall inside the Motherwell box and with his back to the goal, the New Zealander produced a cheeky backheel that flew past Paulsen.

Randall had another chance at the start of the second half but this time his composure deserted him and he blasted well over the bar.

Longelo then found himself in a promising position but his curling shot was deflected for a corner.

The hosts hit back with Bennie cutting in from the left before striking a fierce shot that was well blocked by Motherwell defender Martin Moorman.

There was a big scare for the hosts in the 62nd minute when Bert Esselink was robbed of possession by Seb Palmer-Houlden but the striker’s shot flew just over.

It was United’s turn to threaten next with Michael Forbes producing a powerful header that was cleared off the line by Moorman.

The hosts had a great chance to snatch a winner in the 87th minute but Josh Rawlins completely fluffed his lines just two yards with Randall then coming close with a shot.

#2249. Lazio, Tavares fuori dai convocati del Portogallo dopo l’infortunio

Il terzino si è fermato contro il Napoli: salterà le gare del 14 novembre con la Danimarca e del 17 con il Galles.

Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, Nuno Tavares non risponderà alla convocazione del Portogallo. Il terzino della Lazio si è infortunato nella partita contro il Napoli e il problema fisico gli impedirà di raggiungere la nazionale guidata da Jorge Jesus.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Tavares salterà i prossimi due impegni del Portogallo: la sfida del 14 novembre contro la Danimarca e quella del 17 novembre contro il Galles. Il forfait del biancoceleste ha reso necessario un cambio nell’elenco dei convocati.

Al posto di Tavares, Jorge Jesus ha scelto Flavio Nazinho, terzino classe 2003 dell’AS Monaco. Per il ventitreenne si tratta della prima convocazione con la nazionale maggiore portoghese.

Arrivato nel Principato dal Cercle Brugge durante l’ultima estate, Nazinho si è imposto rapidamente tra le sorprese di questo inizio di stagione in Ligue 1.

#2248. Gattuso: “Vi racconto cosa successe prima di Napoli-Verona, un dolore uguale a quello in Nazionale”

L’allenatore della Lazio Rino Gattuso ha parlato in conferenza stampa nel post-partita di Napoli-Lazio. Ecco quanto sottolineato da IamNaples.it:

“Non sono incazzato, anzi nello spogliatoio a fine partita c’era un po’ di rammarico, non bisogna essere rammaricati. Oggi era una partita trappola, giocavamo contro una squadra ferita, forte nonostante le dieci-dodici assenze. È un punto che ci teniamo stretto, venire qui non è mai facile, il Napoli in questo momento è pieno d’orgoglio, allenata da un tecnico che ha vinto tantissimo. Abbiamo avuto grandissimo coraggio andando sui riferimenti e accettando la profondità, loro facevano fatica a rientrare, abbiamo sofferto un po’ di transizioni attaccando con tanti calciatori. A Nuno bisogna fare i complimenti per la disponibilità, non si è allenato in questa settimana, smaltiva una contrattura al flessore, sapevamo che poteva lasciarci in qualsiasi momento. Sutalo non andrà in Nazionale e vedremo che grado di lesione avrà, forse Cancellieri poteva fare qualcosa in più ma non è abituato a giocare a sinistra. Gudmunsson può fare tanti ruoli, il falso nove, il sottopunta, aspettiamo la risonanza di martedì-mercoledi per Zaccagni. Secondo tempo? È stata la bravura del Napoli, hanno grande fisicità, veemenza e ci sta che soffri una squadra come il Napoli ma non siamo usciti dalla partita, abbiamo tenuto botta. Una settimana fa contro il Cagliari i subentranti ci hanno fatto vincere la partita, oggi era una partita difficile, se giocavamo palla centrale loro recuperavano palla e potevano ripartire, dovevamo essere più bravi a giocare sulle catene. Belahyane ha fatto una buona partita, Lang ci ha messo in difficoltà. Napoli-Verona? Il dolore è più o meno uguale a quello vissuto in Nazionale, eravamo partiti male, perdiamo a Verona, meritavo di essere cacciato e fortunatamente non l’ha fatto, abbiamo ottenuto 14 vittorie e 4 pareggi. Si è parlato di tutto tranne che di quella partita, siamo arrivati scarichi, il presidente è venuto un’ora e venti, un’ora e mezza prima, si doveva parlare di premi e non l’ha fatto. Ho lasciato un pizzico di cuore, stavo bene, mi trovavo a mio agio, il rammarico più grande è che saremmo arrivati secondi, avremmo fatto un’impresa. Oggi ero geloso, eravamo in pieno Covid, si giocava con lo stadio vuoto, è una bellezza incredibile. Floriani? Con i dati che ha, la fisicità che ha può fare qualsiasi cosa, è un Iron Man. Sta sul pezzo, vuole sempre migliorarsi, ha grandissima voglia”

Dal nostro inviato al Maradona Ciro Troise

#2247. Cisse: "Il PSV mi voleva subito, ma il Milan... Amorim sa tenermi con i piedi per terra"

Alphadjo Cisse è l'uomo del momento in casa Milan. Il fantasista dei rossoneri è stato convocato anche da Mancini in Nazionale e ha raccontato com'è andata la prima grande decisione della sua vita calcistica: "Il gruppo WhatsApp dei miei amici era esploso: 'Alpha, ma è vero?!'. E io: 'Sì ragazzi, sì!'. Non volevo sbagliare la scelta: il PSV mi voleva subito, mentre il Milan mi avrebbe lasciato terminare la stagione in Serie B. Due grandi squadre, ma il Milan… come lo spieghi? Vivevo un mix di emozioni, i miei genitori - spiega a Cronache di Spogliatoio - mi hanno detto di stare tranquillo e che il meglio stava per arrivare. Abbiamo deciso che questa era la scelta giusta. E vedendo come sta andando, direi che abbiamo avuto ragione".

Ci racconti il suo primo mese al Milan. "Le prime volte in cui sono venuto a Milanello, l'ho fatto per curarmi dall'infortunio. Il Milan mi ha lasciato a Catanzaro, sì, ma dopo pochi giorni mi sono fatto male. Infatti avevo dei grandi dubbi: 'Arrivo al Milan dopo un infortunio, vediamo come va'. Proprio di questo mi ha parlato Amorim appena ci siamo visti: ci siamo concentrati sull'infortunio, mi ha spiegato cosa si aspettava da me in campo. È una bella persona, che con noi giovani ci sa fare. E sa tenermi con i piedi per terra. Anche se non sono una persona a cui piace volare con la mente".

#2246. Lazio e Gattuso, da 45,4 milioni spesi a 105 stimati per cinque giocatori

Noslin conta già quattro gol e quattro assist in 11 partite; per Isaksen la valutazione ipotizzata è di 30 milioni.

La Lazio avrebbe speso 45,4 milioni di euro per cinque giocatori che oggi vengono stimati complessivamente circa 105 milioni. Il confronto riguarda Tijjani Noslin, Gustav Isaksen, Reda Belahyane, Oliver Provstgaard e Romano Floriani Mussolini. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, La cifra d’acquisto presuppone che siano maturate tutte le condizioni per il pagamento dei bonus; quella attuale è una valutazione ipotetica, non il prezzo di cessioni concordate.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La crescita dei cinque viene collegata anche al lavoro di Gennaro Gattuso. La Lazio capolista è descritta come una squadra la cui forza sta soprattutto nel gruppo e nella volontà di vincere insieme, seguendo la richiesta del tecnico. Gattuso non si è lamentato dei giocatori a disposizione e ha lavorato per migliorare anche chi in passato aveva deluso le aspettative. Ai progressi dei singoli si aggiunge la fiducia ricevuta dall’allenatore.

Il cambiamento più evidente riguarda Reda Belahyane. In estate il centrocampista non riusciva neppure a completare gli allenamenti e arrivava da stagioni difficili. Ora è considerato un elemento insostituibile nel centrocampo della squadra che guida la Serie A.

Anche Tijjani Noslin ha migliorato il proprio rendimento. In 11 partite ha realizzato quattro gol e fornito quattro assist, facendo già meglio rispetto ai due precedenti campionati disputati nella Capitale. Il confronto tra la Lazio della scorsa stagione e quella attuale mette in risalto quanto sia cambiato il contributo di giocatori come loro.

Oliver Provstgaard è diventato un punto fermo della difesa e ha conquistato una titolarità che prima non aveva avuto in biancoceleste. Per Gustav Isaksen, invece, non erano in discussione classe e qualità, ma la continuità. Gattuso lo ha aspettato quando non era nelle condizioni migliori, poi lo ha inserito lasciandogli ampia libertà di creare.

Il percorso di Romano Floriani Mussolini parte dalla crescita nella Lazio e passa attraverso i prestiti. Alla Cremonese, retrocessa in Serie B, era stato spesso una riserva; oggi occupa stabilmente la fascia destra all’Olimpico.

Da questa selezione restano fuori Mandas, Frattesi, Taylor e Zaccagni. Nella valutazione proposta, per il portiere viene attribuito un ruolo più importante al lavoro dello staff. Per gli altri tre, le qualità già possedute avrebbero reso più semplice l’intervento di Gattuso.

#2245. Scudetto, quote Lazio a 9,50: Roma davanti, Milan e Como dietro

La squadra di Gasperini scende a 3,75 dopo il Sassuolo; Milan e Como sono entrambi proposti a 11,00.

La Lazio capolista è terza nelle quote per lo scudetto, offerta a 9,50. Secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews, Il pareggio a Napoli ha confermato l’imbattibilità dei biancocelesti, ma per i bookmaker la favorita resta l’Inter, davanti anche alla Roma. È il quadro delle valutazioni riportate da Agipronews dopo l’undicesima giornata.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La squadra biancoceleste ha raccolto nove vittorie e due pareggi nelle prime undici partite di campionato. Anche la trasferta di Napoli si è chiusa senza una sconfitta e la Lazio conserva il primo posto in classifica.

Nelle valutazioni sul tricolore, però, la capolista occupa il terzo gradino: il suo successo finale è fissato a 9,50, alle spalle di Inter e Roma.

La vittoria contro il Como ha rafforzato la posizione dell’Inter nelle quote scudetto. I nerazzurri, secondi in classifica, hanno reagito alla sconfitta nel derby: il secondo titolo consecutivo è proposto a 1,65 su William Hill.

Segue la Roma di Gasperini, ancora imbattuta in campionato e distante due punti dalla vetta. Dopo il successo sul Sassuolo, terzo consecutivo in Serie A, la quota dei giallorossi è scesa da 5,00 a 3,75 su 888sport.

#2243. St Johnstone 2-1 Dundee: Hosts edge derby thriller with deflected winner

A deflected Kai Fotheringham strike on 72 minutes dealt Dundee their first defeat at St Johnstone for five years.

Josh Campbell scored the second headed goal of his loan from Hibernian to earn Saints a fifth-minute lead.

Substitute striker Joe Westley seized on a defensive howler to level just after halftime.

Fotheringham capped an excellent return from a two-match suspension to secure a 2-1 victory with his first goal since William Hill Premiership opening weekend.

Simo Valakari’s side won their fourth league game since returning to the top-flight and moved level on 17 points with their Tayside rivals.

Owen Bevan returned from injury to replace Joe Wright in Steven Pressley’s only change.

Reece McAlear’s illness forced Valakari into one of four switches that also included top-scorer Josh Fowler dropping to the bench.

Danny Schmidt recovered from an ankle knock to lead the line as Saints set the tone with a high-tempo and profitable opening spell.

Bosnian full-back Enes Alic swung over a terrific delivery to the near post. No Dundee defender was wise to the ghosting run of Campbell who arrived on cue to head emphatically past Owen Goodman.

Saints defender Bozo Mikulic was forced off with a facial knock on 14 minutes. Dan Finlayson replaced the Croatian and that defensive switch was not put under great strain in the first 45.

Dundee threatened only in the 24th minute when captain Ethan Hamilton’s surprise shot on the turn was diverted for a corner by Ross Sinclair.

Saints could easily have doubled their advantage three minutes before half-time. Alic conjured a fierce hit from 25 yards, parried out by Goodman. The rebound fell for Taylor Steven who snatched at the ball and shot well wide.

That missed opportunity came back to haunt the Saints quickly after the interval.

Finlayson ushered a header back towards Sinclair but, as the keeper came to gather, a collision with Cheick Diabate caused a spillage.

Westley, one of three halftime introductions, accepted the gift and found the empty net with ease. Saints, as they have done all season, responded well to a setback. Campbell went close at the near post and a full-stretch Goodman’s fingertips brushed a 30-yard dig from Cotterill just wide.

They wrested back the lead with a terrific transition move. Hamilton gave the ball away and Saints swiftly broke. After great work from Liam Smith down the right, Campbell’s blocked effort spun up for Fotheringham.

His shot took a heavy deflection to leave Goodman rooted to the spot as the ball sailed in.

Dundee had the ball in the net through Ryan Finnigan on 79 minutes. However, referee David Dickinson penalised Owen Bevan for a push in the penalty box melee.

And an offside flag denied Macaulay Tait a tap-in third for Saints. Dundee spurned one fine chance at an equaliser in stoppage time.

Westley scuffed his attempt from six yards, and Sinclair was relieved to gather.

#2241. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Possession: Crystal Palace 28%-72% Manchester CityShots: 9-18Shots on target: 1-9Corners: 2-6Touches in the opposition box: 13-33

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#2240. Doveri vince il premio Bulgarelli, premiato anche Grassadonia della Lazio

Il tecnico biancoceleste riceve il riconoscimento per il calcio femminile; l’arbitro parla ai giovani colleghi.

Daniele Doveri ha ricevuto il premio Bulgarelli Number 8 come miglior arbitro. Tra i vincitori della stagione 2025-2026 c’è anche Gianluca Grassadonia della Lazio, premiato tra gli allenatori per il calcio femminile. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, La cerimonia si svolge al Comune di Bologna.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Ricevendo il riconoscimento, Doveri ha ricordato di essere l’arbitro con più presenze in Serie A, oltre che il più esperto e il più anziano anagraficamente. Per questo considera suo compito «dare l'esempio sul terreno di gioco» e trasmettere la propria esperienza ai giovani arbitri che si affacciano alla Serie B e alla Serie A, affinché prosegua il processo di rinnovamento.

Il premio porta il nome dello storico numero 8 del Bologna, tra i fondatori dell’Aic-Associazione italiana calciatori, che organizza l’iniziativa. Doveri si è detto orgoglioso di ricevere un riconoscimento intitolato a Bulgarelli. Ha ricordato il calciatore come «una persona estremamente eretta» e ha aggiunto: «recuperare i valori di una volta e proiettarli nel futuro è la chiave».

Per il calcio maschile, il premio tra gli allenatori è andato a Cesc Fàbregas del Como, intervenuto con un videomessaggio di ringraziamento. Grassadonia è stato invece scelto per il calcio femminile.

Tra i calciatori sono stati premiati Kenan Yildiz della Juventus e Martina Rosucci, rispettivamente come miglior calciatore e miglior calciatrice. Rosucci ha inviato al pubblico un videomessaggio. Alla cerimonia sono presenti Fabio Capello, presidente del premio, Umberto Calcagno, presidente dell’Aic, Maurizio Fabbri, presidente dell’Assemblea legislativa dell’Emilia-Romagna, e Roberta Li Calzi, assessora allo Sport del Comune di Bologna.

#2239. The tactical 'freedom' Celtic give Callum Osmand and his unlikely Camilo Duran bond

With Celtic a goal behind against Besiktas in the 60th minute, on came Callum Osmand. His impact was almost instantaneous, equalising with his first touch and, soon after, setting up fellow substitute Camilo Duran with a refined reverse pass.

Martin O'Neill said it was all part of the masterplan. The Celtic manager rotated his XI heavily before calling on the cavalry come the hour.

Osmand's influence on the 3-2 victory was profound. He enthused the home support with fresh attacking impetus, haring at Besiktas' defence and providing that crucial end product.

Although Osmand averages a goal or assist every 90 minutes this season, he concedes he must improve.

"I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally, and there's stuff I need to tidy up on, decision-making and all this stuff," Osmand said. "But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

"So on a personal note, that's what I want to do, just keep learning and keep understanding my role, like the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

"And I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning, but I feel like when you get thrown in at the deep end, it's the best way to learn, and the worst games are what you learn off more than the good games.

"It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on."

Osmand joined Celtic from Fulham last summer as a central striker, yet since the defeat to Benfica last month, he's been moulded into a left winger.

Learning a new position isn't easy, though Osmand likes the freedom that comes with playing out wide.

"It is new for me, but I'm really enjoying it," he said. "It's a really fun position and it's very, very attacking.

"I have a lot of freedom and the staff give me that freedom and tell me to go and try and make something happen. So it's a great feeling when you know you can just go and sort of impose your game."

Osmand did exactly that on Thursday evening. O'Neill told him to 'just go' before coming on, instructing the 20-year-old to bring the energy that gets supporters on their feet.

"I think that's the best feeling in football, when you can get everyone behind you and it feels amazing, so that's what I sort of strive for, that feeling," Osmand said.

His presence helped flip the game on its head, offering Celtic fresh hope of Europa League progression after defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica, and Celta Vigo.

O'Neill's side can look ahead to their trip to Torreense later this month knowing it means something.

"For us, it felt like a must win, that was our sort of mindset going into that. This was sort of it," Osmand said of the Besiktas game. "Like we knew we could still qualify, but we knew we had to get something out of Thursday night, and I think the boys done amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this.

"We have some tougher away ties, but hopefully we can use that and just use this, and that gives us confidence to play more free, and take more risks.

"Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play, but as you can see, when we're confident, it just goes forward every time, and it's a good feeling, so hopefully we can build on that."

For Celtic, wins like Thursday's have proven rare this season. There was a real sense of togetherness at the full-time whistle.

O'Neill raised his right fist to the heavens in celebration before gracing the turf and embracing his players.

Osmand knows Celtic haven't been at their best of late. Last weekend's defeat at Falkirk sparked some all too familiar emotions.

Thursday sent Celtic to the other end of the spectrum. Now they must stay there.

"I think we know that we're a good side," Osmand said. "We all back each other, and I think when we're all together, and the fans are with us, and you feel it, you just want to get everyone sort of on one page, and then we feel like an amazing team.

"It's sometimes tough to get to that point, because we're lacking confidence, or we're not playing as well, but I think Thursday night really showed everyone was together, and the final whistle gave us that. It should give us that confidence to go on."

Osmand dovetailed superbly with Duran after coming on against Besiktas, setting up the Colombian striker's first goal of the triumph.

That relationship extends beyond the pitch, even if a language barrier remains.

On Duran, Osmand said: "He's unbelievable, a really top player. You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

"I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy.

"His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot. I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

"And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy."

You wouldn't bet against Duran and Osmand once again coming to the fore when Celtic host Kilmarnock in the William Hill Premiership on Sunday afternoon.

The champions defeated Neil McCann's side 5-1 at Rugby Park back in August. A similar result would go a long way to building on the positive feeling triggered by Thursday's victory.

"I think sometimes when you don't give a team that's obviously not doing as well respect, then you can get caught, and sometimes you don't want to get too overconfident going into these games, because then you'll get caught out," Osmand added.

"I think it's just giving every team you play respect, and knowing that most teams can hurt us, and we have to just go in with the same mentality as Thursday night, and hopefully get a good result.

"I think it's really important for the league. Obviously, we're still at the top of the league, but obviously the gap can change at any time, so it's just about winning every game possible in the league, and just building on everything."

#2238. Sopravvissuto a Crans-Montana, Dos Santos lascia il Metz e riparte dalla Ligue 3

Una nuova opportunità calcistica dopo aver vissuto un autentico dramma. Tahirys Dos Santos, difensore franco-capoverdiano di 20 anni rimasto gravemente ferito nell'incendio di Crans-Montana, è ufficialmente un nuovo giocatore dell'US Thionville Lusitanos. Il club francese ha annunciato il suo arrivo in prestito dal Metz fino al termine della stagione 2026/27. Il terzino sinistro giocherà in Ligue 3 sotto la guida dell'allenatore Julien François, con l'obiettivo di ritrovare continuità dopo mesi particolarmente difficili. Cresciuto nel settore giovanile del Metz, dove era approdato a soli otto anni dopo i primi passi nell'ES Longuyon, Dos Santos avrà così la possibilità di proseguire il proprio percorso professionale.

La sua carriera aveva subito una brusca interruzione nella notte tra il 31 dicembre 2025 e il 1° gennaio 2026, quando un devastante incendio aveva colpito un locale di Crans-Montana, in Svizzera. Dos Santos, all'epoca diciannovenne, era stato tra le 115 persone rimaste ferite nella tragedia, riportando ustioni su circa il 30% del corpo. Dopo il ricovero ospedaliero e un lungo percorso di recupero, il giovane difensore era riuscito a riprendere gradualmente l'attività calcistica.

Il trasferimento rappresenta un passaggio importante nella ripresa sportiva del calciatore. Al Thionville, Dos Santos potrà cercare spazio e minuti in campo, lasciandosi progressivamente alle spalle un'esperienza drammatica. Un nuovo inizio per il giovane cresciuto nel Metz, che torna a concentrarsi sul proprio futuro nel calcio professionistico.

#2237. Rrahmani in conferenza stampa: “Siamo stati sempre con Allegri, abbiamo dato tutto in campo”

Amir Rrahmani ha rilasciato queste dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa:

“Nel primo tempo abbiamo avuto tante difficoltà, perché avevano loro tanto spazio in contropiede. Anche per errori nostri. Mentre nella ripresa abbiamo dominato e potevamo vincere. Abbiamo dato tutto in campo, anche se non abbiamo vinto, e di questo ne sono orgoglio. Tutta la ripresa l’abbiamo giocata bene, poi ci sono anche gli avversari: la Lazio è la prima in classifica, hanno la pazienza di aspettare e ripartire. Nel secondo tempo siamo stati bravi a non farli ripartire. Dobbiamo ripartire da questa ripresa. Siamo stati sempre con l’allenatore, che ha vinto tutto in carriera. Crediamo in lui, possiamo uscire da questa competizione così difficile. Dobbiamo credere in quello che facciamo ogni giorno, ci sono stati infortuni. Abbiamo fatto nove partite in un mese ed è stato molto difficile e stancante. Abbiamo dato comunque tutto. Siamo ancora nelle tre competizioni. Quando subisci gol non è solo colpa della difesa, ma di tutta la squadra. Abbiamo preso tanti gol e non siamo abituati a questo, ma stiamo migliorando. Siamo in attesa del ritorno di diversi calciatori, sperando di non perderne altri”.

#2236. Lazio e Roma non lo confermarono: D'Uffizi dall’Ascoli alla Nazionale

Il 22enne è stato convocato nell’Under 21 per le amichevoli con Francia e Belgio dopo l’indisponibilità di Vavassori.

Simone D'Uffizi è stato convocato per la prima volta nella Nazionale Under 21. L’8 novembre 2026 Silvio Baldini lo ha chiamato al raduno di Tirrenia, dopo l’indisponibilità di Dominic Vavassori, per le amichevoli contro Francia e Belgio. Secondo quanto riportato da Gazzetta Regionale, Oggi il 22enne è un punto di riferimento dell’Ascoli; da bambino, invece, Roma e Lazio non lo avevano confermato perché ritenevano troppo esile la sua struttura fisica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

D'Uffizi muove i primi passi nella Breda, società romana in cui si mette presto in evidenza. A nove anni attira gli osservatori della Roma, ma il padre preferisce aspettare. L’ingresso nel vivaio giallorosso arriva due anni dopo, anche grazie all’interessamento di Bruno Conti.

L’esperienza alla Roma si interrompe presto. D'Uffizi passa alla Lazio, ritrova Leonardo Fratangeli e indossa anche la fascia da capitano. Neppure il club biancoceleste, però, lo conferma: il ragazzo torna così alla Breda, la squadra da cui era partito.

Nell’ottobre 2026, ripensando a quel periodo, l’attaccante ha raccontato di aver vissuto entrambe le esclusioni come colpi difficili da assorbire. Nella sua ricostruzione, a pesare era soprattutto il fisico ancora troppo esile. Dopo il ritorno alla Breda aveva persino pensato di smettere, incerto che il calcio potesse restare qualcosa di più di un divertimento.

Il cammino prosegue lontano dai vivai di Roma e Lazio. D'Uffizi passa alla Lodigiani e poi alla Nuova Florida, in Serie D, dove comincia a misurarsi con un calcio diverso da quello giovanile. Nel luglio 2021 firma con la Viterbese ed entra tra i professionisti.

Esterno classe 2004 di scuola Lodigiani, in una sfida contro la prima squadra della Fidelis Andria entra a gara in corso e segna due gol in cinque minuti. È un altro episodio del percorso iniziato dopo il ritorno alla Breda.
