#2235. Il tocco di Palladino sul Bologna nei nuovi ruoli di Casale, Ferguson e Odgaard

Il Bologna ha cambiato nettamente passo rispetto all'inizio della stagione: merito di Raffaele Palladino, che ha saputo imporre la propria presenza nel contesto rossoblù elevando le prestazioni di numerosi singoli e dell'economia generale della squadra. A parlare in suo favore ci sono i dati, che vedono gli emiliani aver raccolto ben 16 punti nelle 7 partite di campionato trascorse agli ordini del mister di Mugnano. Una media di 2,29 punti a gara che dietro ha alcuni interventi pratici ben visibili.

In difesa si è rivisto molto più spesso Nicolò Casale, con un ruolo centrale. Non solo in quanto ad importanza, ma proprio come zona di campo: nel mezzo della nuova linea a tre ideata da Palladino, che ha del tutto rimescolato le gerarchie con l'inserimento di Darmian, acquistato ad hoc da svincolato, e Theate da braccetti. Rispetto a un recente passato vissuto da esubero totale nel Bologna, per Casale è stata una svolta e non da poco. Non solo per lui.

Tra i nei più spesso esposti nell'analisi del calciomercato estivo fatto dal Bologna, c'è anche la mancanza di un vero vice-Freuler. Non ha queste caratteristiche per esempio l'argentino Amondarain, pagato una decina di milioni di euro: Palladino è riuscito ad andare oltre questa mancanza studiando funzioni rinnovate per Lewis Ferguson. Lo scozzese, pena anche qualche infortunio di troppo, ha perso un po' di quello smalto che lo faceva pensare da tutti quale perfetto box-to-box. Considerando però la dote tecnica di cui dispone, da playmaker di centrocampo ha ancora tanto da dire. Palladino se n'è accorto e lì lo ha ridisegnato.

La mossa più visibile tra tutte è quella che però ha meno tasso di genialità o paternità totale dello stesso Palladino. Lo spostamento a numero nove di Jens Odgaard è un fenomeno al quale in passato si è già assistito anche con Motta e Italiano, per quanto non in maniera così sistematica. Per spiegarsi: per Palladino, Odgaard è la prima punta titolare anche in presenza dei vari Piccoli, Enem e Dovbyk. Tutti e tre acquistati sul mercato estivo, ma scavalcati dall'adattamento del danese.

#2234. Allegri: “Siamo ancora nelle tre competizioni, dopo la sosta recupereremo un po’ di calciatori e miglioreremo”

L’allenatore del Napoli Massimiliano Allegri ha parlato nel post-partita di Napoli-Lazio. Ecco quanto sottolineato da IamNaples.it:

“Sono contento della prestazione dei ragazzi per novanta minuti, nel primo tempo abbiamo avuto delle situazioni favorevoli. La squadra ha fatto un bel secondo tempo, la cosa positiva è che siamo rimasti ordinati per novanta minuti. Sarebbe stato doloroso perdere oggi, invece, i ragazzi hanno fatto quello che potevano fare come hanno sempre fatto. In questo momento non siamo riusciti a vincere, dopo la sosta recupereremo un po’ di giocatori e credo che faremo bene. Siamo ancora nella Coppa Italia, in Champions League, in campionato siamo ancora in corsa per i primi quattro posti anche se siamo un po’ indietro. Oggi in modo molto semplice siamo stati un filo più ordinati, nella parte sinistra nel primo tempo non riuscivamo a prendere le contromisure tra Vergara e Beukema. Potevamo essere meno frenetici in certi momenti della gara, Lang è un ragazzo che secondo me ha delle qualità importanti, ha fatto una buona prestazione, deve crescere in responsabilità sapendo che ogni pallone può essere decisivo per la partita. Ha messo dei buoni cross nel secondo tempo e, infatti, siamo stati più incisivi. Per esperienza e per carattere, credo che a tutte le problematiche ci sia una soluzione, i ragazzi stanno facendo il possibile. Ci mancano dei calciatori non solo in partita ma anche durante gli allenamenti, non sono alibi, scuse, dobbiamo essere bravi a rovesciare le situazioni. Riprenderemo sabato a lavorare, ho parlato con De Laurentiis, credo che anche lui abbia chiaro la realtà delle cose, sa che ci sono delle difficoltà oggettive. Ci deve essere da parte di tutti una presa di coscienza, credo che ci sia da parte del presidente e della società, i giocatori meritano di essere difesi. Lucca è stato acquistato dal Napoli, quando l’hanno preso hanno visto delle qualità, se ce l’aveva prima ce l’ha anche ora. Ha avuto poi delle situazioni favorevoli che magari fra 20 giorni sfrutterà meglio, finchè ci metteranno cuore e passione, possono sbagliare anche tecnicamente, non ci sono vagabondi. Milinkovic? Sono due portieri di grande valore, ha fatto una bella partita e con i piedi, ha fornito due assist importanti, è un portiere molto bravo e poi una persona affidabile”

#2232. Calò e la mancata convocazione in Nazionale, Mancini: "quando servirà lo faremo ma non perché ce lo dicono i procuratori"

Il ct riconosce le prestazioni del centrocampista del Frosinone, ma chiarisce il criterio seguito per le convocazioni.

Giacomo Calò è seguito dalla Nazionale, ma Roberto Mancini non lo ha convocato per il raduno di Coverciano. Il commissario tecnico riconosce il buon momento del centrocampista del Frosinone, allenato da Massimiliano Alvini. Secondo quanto riportato da figc, A 29 anni, però, Calò non rientra tra i giocatori che il ct vuole osservare in questa fase, dedicata soprattutto ai più giovani.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Gli Azzurri si sono ritrovati a Coverciano la sera dell’8 novembre 2026. Nel pomeriggio del 9 novembre è prevista la prima seduta di allenamento verso le ultime due partite del girone di Nations League, contro Francia e Belgio. Nella conferenza stampa di inizio raduno, Mancini ha affrontato anche il tema delle convocazioni e delle prospettive della squadra. La FIGC riporta le sue dichiarazioni.

Mancini considera Calò uno dei giocatori che stanno facendo bene e che la Nazionale tiene sotto osservazione. Il ct ha aggiunto che nel Frosinone ci sono altri tre o quattro elementi validi. La scelta per questo raduno, tuttavia, segue un criterio diverso: «Ma non possiamo chiamare giocatori di 29/30 anni in questa fase, quando servirà lo faremo ma non perché ce lo dicono i procuratori».

Il tecnico ha allargato il discorso allo spazio concesso ai giovani in Serie A. A suo giudizio, la situazione è rimasta più o meno la stessa: alcuni club li impiegano, altri no. Per la Nazionale, ha spiegato, resta l’obbligo di cercare ragazzi da convocare e conoscere direttamente, anche quando sono molto giovani. L’intento è valutarne le qualità tecniche in vista della loro possibile crescita.

La linea seguita dal ct riguarda anche alcuni campioni d’Europa assenti dall’elenco, tra cui Bernardeschi, Chiesa e Cristante. Mancini conosce già Bernardeschi e Cristante e ha detto che potrà richiamarli quando ne avrà bisogno. Con Chiesa ha parlato più volte, anche di recente: il giocatore ora non sta giocando, deve ritrovare la condizione e, secondo il ct, a 29 anni può tornare presto in Nazionale.

Mancini ha confermato sei dei nove volti nuovi visti nella finestra di settembre e ottobre: Ghilardi, Kayode, Romano, Doumbia, Sebastiano Esposito e Vergara. Ha richiamato Ahanor e accolto dall’Under 21 Pisilli e Koleosho. Parlando del loro passaggio, ha ricordato il buon rapporto con Baldini e gli ha augurato di vincere l’Europeo.

Tra le prime convocazioni figurano due giocatori del Como di Fabregas: Mattia Liberali, classe 2007, e Riccardo Cassano, classe 2009. Nell’elenco c’è anche Alphadjo Cisse, attaccante del Milan nato nel 2006. La sua chiamata era nell’aria: l’8 novembre ha segnato per la quinta volta in Serie A ed è il miglior marcatore rossonero. Completano le novità il difensore dell’Udinese Matteo Palma e Simone Lontani, del Parma, entrambi classe 2008.

Palma, Liberali e Cisse resteranno con il gruppo per tutto il raduno. Cassano e Lontani si alleneranno per alcuni giorni a Coverciano, poi raggiungeranno rispettivamente le Nazionali Under 18 e Under 19. La prima è impegnata nel Mondiale al via il 19 novembre in Qatar; la seconda nella fase delle qualificazioni europee in programma dall’11 al 17 novembre nelle Marche. Mancini li ha chiamati anche per conoscerli e osservarli da vicino.

Il ct ha detto che tutti i giovani presenti gli hanno dato buone sensazioni. Di Liberali ha sottolineato le qualità e il percorso nelle giovanili, pur ricordando le poche presenze in Serie A. Lontani lo aveva colpito già alla prima di campionato: a suo giudizio è migliorato partita dopo partita e il gol contro l’Atalanta ne conferma personalità e doti tecniche.

Palma, che era in bilico tra Italia e Germania, può diventare secondo Mancini un difensore molto bravo. Cisse può ricoprire entrambi i ruoli d’attacco e il ct vuole vederlo al lavoro. Cassano è un regista di centrocampo: deve crescere fisicamente, ma Mancini ne apprezza la lettura del gioco e ritiene che possa diventare importante per il futuro azzurro.

Un’altra scelta tra Italia e Germania riguarda Nicolò Tresoldi. Mancini e Ranieri hanno parlato con lui, ma il ct ha ribadito che la decisione spetta al giocatore. Tresoldi è nato in Italia e suo padre ha giocato per la Nazionale, vincendo l’Europeo Under 21. Per Mancini ci sono possibilità che scelga gli Azzurri, con i quali potrebbe avere un ruolo importante.

#2231. Calvarese risponde a Rabiot: "Normale la pensi così". La spiegazione su Genoa-Milan

Gianpaolo Calvarese sdrammatizza sul caso Genoa-Milan e risponde a livello tecnico alle rimostranze social di Adrien Rabiot: "Credo sia del tutto normale che Rabiot la veda in questa maniera. Un calciatore si occupa del campo ed è giusto che magari non conosca tutti i parametri e abbia la sua idea", ha detto Calvarese a TuttoMercatoWeb.com. "Adrien lo saluto, con lui ci siamo sempre confrontati e con lui ho un ottimo rapporto, poi ho risposto tecnicamente".

Il caso è noto ed è uno dei più discussi del weekend arbitrale: Rabiot si invola in campo aperto, Marcandalli lo atterra da ultimo uomo e si vede mostrare solo il giallo. Rispondendo alla spiegazione data da Calvarese sull'episodio (su Instagram) Rabiot aveva scritto all'ex arbitro: "Nella vita come nel calcio si possono fare errori, bisogna almeno saperli ammettere. Mentire continuamente non vi farà andare avanti. Ed è il calcio italiano a subirne le conseguenze.. Pensateci. Bonne soirée".

Contattato dalla nostra redazione, Calvarese riporta quella che è stata la versione che è possibile ascoltare anche nel podcast "Gian&Giac" sul suo canale YouTube "calVAResegianpaolo": "Mi son sentito di dire, appoggiandomi al regolamento, che per essere chiara ed evidente - così dice il regolamento - l'occasione da gol deve rispettare tutti e 4 i parametri previsti per il rosso. Ho detto che era sostenibile la scelta dell'arbitro".

Questa la spiegazione: "I quattro parametri da rispettare sono: la probabilità di mantenere o guadagnare il controllo del pallone, il numero dei difendenti, la direzione generale dell'azione e la distanza dalla porta. Siamo a 60-65 metri dalla porta. Sicuramente un'occasione da gol, sicuramente se avesse dato rosso non sarebbe intervenuto il VAR, sicuramente una decisione difficile. A livello geografico, visto che siamo in questa posizione, ho detto per questo che fosse una scelta sostenibile".

#2230. Sam Johnstone's honest Celtic results admission as dressing room mood revealed

Goalkeeper Sam Johnstone admits Celtic have fallen below expectations this season, with recent form impacting the team's spirit.

Thursday's 3-2 victory over Besiktas, Johnstone says, showed their character, with the long-term target now to 'put things right'.

The stopper, signed on loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers during the summer transfer window, has started Celtic's last five matches, displacing Viljami Sinisalo between the sticks.

"The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games," Johnstone said. "Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation, and the lads know that. We try to win every game and put things right."

Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone walks off the pitch at half-time. (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Celtic had won just three of their previous ten matches before Besiktas.

Beating the Turks, then, was crucial in repairing the mood, both internally and externally.

"I think the results affect it," Johnstone said of the spirit within the camp. "This club's not used to losing, and we’ve probably lost too many games for this club.

"We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game. The lads go out to win every game, so the camp is good.

"It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people, and honest with each other. You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result."

Johnstone's recent run of starts is his most consistent since joining Celtic at the start of September.

The 33-year-old was thrust in shortly after signing, playing against St Johnstone in the William Hill Premiership and Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup.

He failed to impress in the 3-0 defeat at Ibrox but now looks far more assured.

"To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm," Johnstone explained. "It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

"Listen, to get the games and to keep going and get the win on Thursday night was a good feeling.

"It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

"When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here."

After their first Europa League win of the season, Celtic's focus shifts back to the domestic scene, where Kilmarnock lie in wait on Sunday afternoon.

Returning to winning ways in the Premiership after last weekend's defeat to Falkirk is key.

#2229. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

"Incredible talent." 🌟Steven Gerrard reacts to Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola.🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/bVd7odopa3

"It was the shared vision." 🤝Oliver Glasner on why he chose to join the Nottingham Forest project 👀 pic.twitter.com/ldxjwU8FW4

"For me, it's a special game, definitely." ❤️Andoni Iraola looks ahead to his first Premier League game at Anfield as Liverpool boss.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fukilMigKz

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2228. Taylor della Lazio non convocato dall’Olanda: Xavi spiega la scelta

Il selezionatore considera la sua esclusione la decisione più difficile e richiama la concorrenza a centrocampo.

Kenneth Taylor non è stato convocato dall’Olanda per i prossimi impegni internazionali. In conferenza stampa, il selezionatore Xavi ha definito la sua esclusione la decisione più difficile nella composizione della lista. La scelta arriva dopo le prime 11 presenze in Serie A del centrocampista con la Lazio, nelle quali ha segnato 2 gol e fornito 2 assist.

Nel suo primo scorcio di stagione in biancoceleste, l’ex Ajax ha contribuito con 2 reti e 2 assist nelle prime 11 uscite di campionato. Il suo rendimento è stato al centro delle domande rivolte a Xavi durante la presentazione dei prossimi appuntamenti dell’Olanda.

Il selezionatore ha riconosciuto le prestazioni del centrocampista in Italia, pur avendo scelto di non inserirlo nell’attuale lista dei convocati.

Xavi ha spiegato quanto sia stata complessa la decisione: «L’esclusione di Kenneth Taylor è stata in assoluto la decisione più difficile che ho dovuto prendere per questa lista di convocati». Nel reparto, ha aggiunto, l’Olanda dispone di molti centrocampisti di livello.

Secondo il selezionatore, quanto mostrato da Taylor avrebbe giustificato una convocazione. Il giocatore della Lazio resta comunque tra i profili seguiti in vista dei prossimi impegni della Nazionale olandese.

#2227. Gattuso a DAZN: “Pareggiare al Maradona non era facile, sono orgoglioso dei ragazzi”

Gennaro Gattuso, allenatore della Lazio, è intervenuto ai microfoni di DAZN dopo il pari contro il Napoli: “Il Maradona è un campo difficile, il Napoli è una squadra forte. Guardiamo i giocatori in campo. Nello spogliatoio c’era un mortorio, ma ho fatto i complimenti alla squadra. Va bene, mi piace che siano delusi. Sono orgogliosi dei ragazzi: venire qua, in un momento di difficoltà e con questo stadio non è facile, dobbiamo essere soddisfatti. Voglio più sorrisi. Gol di Frattesi? E’ un ‘capoccione’! Non ce la fa, deve toccare, si fissa. In pochi ce ne sono così in Europa. Stiamo lì ogni giorno col match analyst a studiare con lui. Anche Taylor ha tirato, ma poteva passare a Isaksen. Potevamo fare qualche gol in più, ma ci teniamo la prestazione, sono soddisfatto. La classifica non dobbiamo guardarla, noi c’entriamo poco là. Avranno due giorni liberi, poi riprenderemo e sabato avremo un’amichevole con una squadra maltese. Viviamo alla giornata, giochiamo con sacrificio e coraggio come contro il Napoli. C’erano persone veloci in avanti, ci hanno messo in difficoltà, ma lo abbiamo accettato. E’ mentalità. Partita dopo partita, vedremo. Ora bisogna mettere fieno in cascina. Un punto muove sempre la classifica, dobbiamo ragionare così”.

#2226. Cancellieri, meno spazio alla Lazio: Fiorentina attenta alla scadenza

Una cessione a gennaio consentirebbe ai biancocelesti di ricavare una somma dal cartellino dell'esterno.

Matteo Cancellieri potrebbe tornare nei piani della Fiorentina per il mercato invernale. Secondo quanto riportato da FiorentinaUno, L'esterno offensivo della Lazio, che nelle ultime settimane ha trovato poco spazio, sarebbe nuovamente seguito da Fabio Paratici. Un'eventuale operazione a gennaio resta un'ipotesi, legata anche alle scelte del club biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il futuro a Roma del calciatore italiano, classe 2002, non appare scontato. Cancellieri non sembra più occupare una posizione centrale nelle scelte tecniche della Lazio e sta attraversando una fase complicata, nella quale giocare con continuità è diventato più difficile.

Alla situazione in campo si aggiunge quella contrattuale: l'accordo con i biancocelesti scade il 30 giugno 2027. Senza un rinnovo, la società dovrà decidere come affrontare gli ultimi mesi del rapporto. Anche il giocatore sarà chiamato a valutare quale soluzione possa offrirgli maggiore continuità.

Paratici conosce il profilo di Cancellieri e potrebbe scegliere tra due possibilità. La prima è provare ad anticipare l'operazione a gennaio, cercando un'intesa con la Lazio. L'altra è aspettare la fine della stagione per tentare di ingaggiare l'esterno a parametro zero.

Attendere consentirebbe alla Fiorentina di non sostenere il costo del cartellino, ma potrebbe esporla alla concorrenza di altre società. Non è la prima volta che il nome di Cancellieri viene associato ai viola: nelle precedenti finestre di mercato il club toscano aveva già mostrato interesse, considerandolo una possibile alternativa per il reparto offensivo.

Tra le caratteristiche prese in considerazione c'è la sua duttilità. Cancellieri può giocare soprattutto sulla corsia destra, ma anche in altre posizioni dell'attacco: una possibilità utile nella costruzione della rosa viola, che potrebbe cambiare volto.

#2225. SPFL round-up: Partick Thistle go top as Hamilton stunned by Cove Rangers

Partick Thistle climbed to the top of the William Hill Championship with a 1-0 victory over rock-bottom Queen’s Park.

The moment of the game came 10 minutes after the break when Seb Drozd’s effort deflected to Tony Watt at the far post who headed Thistle to victory and climbed above Raith who drew 0-0 with Dunfermline.

Dylan Borso scored four times as they came from behind to win 4-3 and inflict a fourth straight defeat on Stenhousemuir despite playing more than an hour with a man less after Calvin Okike was sent off for the hosts.

Arbroath ended a run of five-straight defeats in style as they earned a convincing 4-1 win over Ayr courtesy of goals from Thomas O’Brien, Michael McKenna, Gavin Reilly and Jacob MacIntyre.

Cristian Montano’s equaliser cancelled out Alfie Stewart’s opener as Livingston drew 1-1 with Inverness.

In League One, Ross County moved five points clear at the top of the league after they ran out 4-1 winners over Peterhead.

Brian Graham and Chris Hamilton gave County a 2-0 lead before Mitch Megginson pulled a goal back for the visitors but the home side finished the job with further goals from Richard Chin and Kieran Phillips’ penalty.

Second-placed Hamilton suffered a shock first defeat of the season after they were thrashed 4-0 by rock-bottom Cove Rangers thanks to Edimond Oppong’s hat-trick and Joseph Teasdale’s late strike.

Goals from Jamie Hamilton and Cameron Elliott’s penalty helped East Kilbride come from behind and earn a first win four games with a 2-1 victory over Queen of the South.

Cammie Ross struck four minutes from time to give East Fife a second-straight win as they beat Montrose 2-1 who had goalscorer Blair Lyons sent off late.

Airdrieonians ended a run of three consecutive defeats with a 3-2 win over lowly Alloa courtesy of Rangers loanee Josh Gentles’ late goal.

Stranraer remained at the top of League Two with a 3-0 victory over Stirling who saw their five-match league unbeaten run come to an end.

Second-placed Clyde picked up a third win from their last four after they twice came from behind to beat The Spartans 3-2.

Leighton McIntosh and Scott Honeyman gave Dumbarton a first win in four with a 2-0 victory over Elgin.

Jack Brydon’s late strike earned Kelty Hearts a 2-1 win over Annan Athletic while Forfar drew 1-1 with Edinburgh.

#2224. Lega B al Social Football Summit. Bedin: "Posizione centrale sul tema dell'evoluzione del calcio"

La Lega Nazionale Professionisti Serie B punta sulla vetrina del Social Football Summit per una fitta due giorni di eventi istituzionali, commerciali e formativi. Domani, martedì 10 novembre, e mercoledì 11 novembre, lo Juventus Stadium di Torino, sarà il centro nevralgico della più importante manifestazione in Italia dedicata alla social e football industry, ospitando fra gli altri quattro appuntamenti chiave a cui prenderanno parte i club della Serie BKT.

'La partecipazione della Lega Serie B al SFS26 -sottolinea il Presidente Paolo Bedin - conferma la volontà di posizionarsi al centro del dibattito nazionale sull’evoluzione del sistema calcistico, confrontandosi con le tendenze in termini di management, sostenibilità e networking aziendale'.

Dopo l’Assemblea dei club del mattino, prevista alle ore 11, nel pomeriggio la Lega Serie B aprirà le porte ai partecipanti e al pubblico del Summit con due panel nella Sala Legends Nord. Alle ore 15 si terrà l'incontro "La sfida del calcio tra spettacolo e sostenibilità", organizzato da LEAP Sports Academy, focalizzato sulla transizione ecologica e l'impatto sociale dello sport di vertice. Alle 16,15 sarà la volta del talk "Serie BKT: Valori che creano valore - I territori e le opportunità per i Partner", un approfondimento strategico sul legame unico che unisce le piazze della B al tessuto imprenditoriale locale e nazionale con la presenza dei partner ufficiali del campionato.

La mattina di mercoledì 11 novembre (ore 10, Sala Stampa) vedrà un terzo momento di confronto pubblico con il panel "LNPB: evoluzione, status quo e scenari di sviluppo", organizzato in collaborazione con Football Benchmark, volto ad analizzare i dati di sviluppo, gli aspetti socioeconomici e gli scenari strategici del campionato e dei venti club di Serie BKT.

In linea con gli obiettivi di professionalizzazione promossi dal Social Football Summit, la due giorni torinese vedrà inoltre workshop didattici dedicati alla crescita delle figure interne ai club: la mattina sarà riservata alla formazione dei Team Manager, mentre nel pomeriggio la Sala Legends Sud ospiterà l'aggiornamento per i Responsabili Marketing & Comunicazione.

L'intero palinsesto di eventi LNPB all'SFS26 è supportato dall’Event Partner Cattolica Assicurazioni Agenzia Generale Firenze.

#2222. After being benched for Celtic loan star, my on-field response was emphatic

Lucas Clearie has issued another reminder of his goalscoring potential after hitting a first-half hat-trick for Celtic B.

The 17-year-old was benched for the midweek KDM Evolution Trophy clash with Ross County, with Shim Mheuka preferred through the middle.

But Clearie responded in emphatic fashion just four days later with a first-half hat-trick against Beith Juniors. The striker opened the scoring in the 18th minute before adding another in the 42nd minute. He completed his hat-trick in the 45th minute.

His prolific form comes as he attempts to force his way into the thoughts of first-team manager Martin O’Neill.

Clearie was among seven Celtic youngsters handed their first professional contracts in the summer of 2025 and has continued to enhance his reputation with the B team.

The teenager’s latest treble also rounded off an impressive week after he was included alongside Celtic teammate Corey Shaw in the Scotland Under-19 squad.

Scotland are due to face Kazakhstan, Kosovo and Belgium during the international window.

#2221. Totti al Fenerbahçe? Il club turco smentisce ufficialmente: "Notizie completamente infondate"

Nessun futuro al Fenerbahçe per Francesco Totti, almeno secondo quanto comunicato ufficialmente dal club turco. Nelle ultime ore, il quotidiano Sözcü aveva rilanciato l'ipotesi di un ingresso dell'ex capitano della Roma nella dirigenza sportiva della società di Istanbul. Una suggestione che aveva rapidamente attirato l'attenzione dei media locali, anche alla luce del momento complicato attraversato dal Fenerbahçe. Totti, attualmente senza incarichi ufficiali nel mondo del calcio, era stato indicato come una possibile figura di riferimento per rilanciare il progetto sportivo gialloblù. La società, però, ha deciso di intervenire direttamente per smentire la ricostruzione.

Attraverso una nota ufficiale pubblicata lunedì 9 novembre, il club ha respinto categoricamente le indiscrezioni: "Le informazioni pubblicate oggi dal quotidiano Sözcü con il titolo 'Lo spirito calcistico del Fenerbahçe', e successivamente riprese da altri media, secondo cui Francesco Totti sarebbe entrato a far parte della dirigenza sportiva del nostro club, sono completamente infondate". Una presa di posizione netta, accompagnata da un richiamo alla responsabilità degli organi d'informazione.

La società turca ha infatti invitato le testate coinvolte a "rispettare i principi giornalistici e ad agire responsabilmente", criticando la diffusione di notizie prive di riscontri. La smentita ufficiale chiude così, almeno per il momento, le voci su un possibile approdo di Totti al Fenerbahçe in veste dirigenziale.

#2220. St Johnstone boss banishes Dundee demons with ‘bitter’ declaration

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory over Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Dundee won twice at McDiarmid Park in 2024-25, the season Saints were relegated, but a transformed team has returned to the top flight under Valakari.

They drew level on 17 points with Dundee in the William Hill Premiership thanks to a fourth win of the season. Valakari lapped up the success, with fans joyous at a first home victory over the Dark Blues since October 2021.

“We are a totally new team and it is not good to hold on to all those memories,” said Valakari. “Me as a manager, of course I remember. At Christmas-time we were 3-0 down after 20 minutes of the biggest game of the season.

“And of course I remember when their fans were on the pitch celebrating on the last day. But my players don’t have this baggage. We are creating new experiences together; this is our new adventure.

“If I carried everything that happened in the past with me, I would be a very bitter person! You need to let things go; that’s why we didn’t even bring it up.

“But all the players knew how much this game meant to our fans. We needed to perform, and we did. And to perform the way we did against a very good team made it a deserved win.”

Josh Campbell headed Saints in front after five minutes before substitute Joe Westley replied early in the second half following a mix-up between goalkeeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for Saints, netted a deflected winner in the 72nd minute.

“We were very good in the first half,” said Valakari. “They changed things at half-time. It took us a bit of time to adjust and we conceded a goal in that period.

“My team showed their character and personality again. We got control back and it got better and better from that.”

Dundee manager Steven Pressley conceded that his team failed to match much of their early-season form. He admitted St Johnstone were deserving winners over the course of the match.

“Over the course of the 90 minutes, St Johnstone were probably deserving of the victory,” he said. “We didn’t quite reach the heights and the standards that we’ve set.

“It’s not a criticism, it’s just these players continuously produced really high performances and have set some incredible standards. We were just a little bit below them on some of the things that we pride ourselves on.

“And, on the things we pride ourselves on, I thought St Johnstone were very strong. We’re disappointed to go into an international break on a defeat.”

#2219. Sheffield Wednesday told they should have signed Mansfield Town and Bradford City pair in the summer by reporter

Sheffield Wednesday will have the chance to bolster their squad when the January transfer window opens up for business. SWFC are currently positioned in 9th place in the League One table.

Smith, 35, joined Mansfield Town on a free transfer. Meanwhile, Beesley, 29, signed for Bradford City from Burton Albion.

Staton reckons they would have both been ideal for the Owls and has said, as per a report by BBC Sport: “Wednesday missed a trick during the summer. Two players spring to mind — Michael Smith, the former Owl who joined Mansfield, and Jake Beesley who moved from Burton to Bradford.

“Smith was available on a free transfer and would’ve done exactly what Wednesday need – lead the line, frustrate defenders, help the Owls get up the pitch and chip in with goals. He might be 35 now but he can still do a job as he’s showing for the Stags.

“Beesley might’ve been harder to acquire given he joined Bradford for an undisclosed fee. The financial restrictions placed on Wednesday made any signing a challenge over the summer. People will point to the fact he has only one goal for the Bantams so far, but he’s a pain in the neck to play against – big and strong, he batters defenders and can hold it up.”

Sheffield Wednesday fans know all about Smith from his spell at Hillsborough from 2022 to 2025. He made 127 appearances for SWFC in all competitions and scored 33 goals.

He spent the last campaign at Preston North End before he was allowed to leave for Mansfield Town in mid-July. The ex-Swindon Town, Portsmouth and Rotherham United man has since found the net on six occasions in 15 outings for the Stags altogether since his switch to Field Mill.

If he had re-joined the Owls, he would have given them more competition and depth up top. In addition, he could have injected some serious experience into their ranks.

As for Beesley, he has struggled for form since his transfer to Bradford City. He has scored only once for the Bantams in 15 games. He was handed a deal until 2028 by the West Yorkshire club.

The Sheffield-born man was a hit during his time at Burton Albion and was one of their key players. He has also had spells in the past at Chesterfield, Salford City, Solihull Moors, Rochdale and Blackpool and is well travelled.

As Staton has alluded to, Sheffield Wednesday are lacking a proper number nine. SWFC could do with landing a forward this winter.

Smith and Beesley have only just joined Mansfield Town and Bradford City respectively so they are unlikely to be on the Owls’ radar. There are plenty of other options they can identify over the coming weeks though.

Dave Challinor will be eager to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad with some reinforcements. He was picked as the replacement for Henrik Pedersen and will be looking to guide his new team back to the Championship at the first time of asking.

Sheffield Wednesday lost 2-1 away at Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup on Sunday afternoon. They are back in action on Wednesday at home to Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy.
