#2179. Top 15 best away fans in the EFL ranked

When it comes to topics of discourse throughout the EFL sphere, few subjects promise to spark fiercer debate than arguments over which clubs have the best - and worst - away support.

Supporting your team at home is one thing, but committing to pocket-burning expenses and significant mileage travelling up and down the country in the name of fanfare takes on a new level of loyalty and is worn as a badge of honor by the clubs who make a particular impression in terraces on the road.

Factoring in a blend of noise and numbers while giving special attention to the teams that really clock up the miles, Football League World has decided to run the rule and rank the FIFTEEN best-supported clubs away from home in the EFL right now...

We're heading underway with Leicester City, who have always been historically well-followed despite never being a major-hitter in the realms of EFL fanfare.

Leicester's location within the East Midlands means few destinations are "too far", whereas relegation to League One for only the second time in the club's history makes for many interesting away days that, admittedly, supporters never thought they'd be embarking on.

Nonetheless, the Foxes often travel in numbers, are noisy when they're up for it and have already recorded two of the highest away attendances in the EFL this season after taking in excess of 4,000 fans to both Barnsley and MK Dons.

Southampton's fanbase, for all intents and purposes, is rather comparable to the contingent in support of Leicester, though it's the Hampshire outfit who just about gain an edge here.

The Saints' location doesn't always make away travel easy, yet that rarely stops them from bringing swathes of supporters on their trips with a decent atmosphere to boot.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

They posted the sixth-highest average away attendance in the Championship last season, and when those numbers are regularly accompanied by noise despite more arduous mileage than most, it's hard to resist giving Southampton their flowers.

West Bromwich Albion have always retained solid support both home and away amid plenty of local competition within the Black Country and wider West Midlands region, which is why it's only right to recognise their own standing on the road.

Once again, the majority of away trips fail to require lofty travel commitments and the club's West Midlands status makes it easy to reach most destinations by train.

That culminates in consistently respectable numbers with the capacity to make a serious racket when the good times are rolling or a local derby arrives, but whilst only six sides travelled better than the Baggies last term, the fact that multiple fellow Midlands clubs did prevents Albion from featuring higher.

Bolton Wanderers' support has been tested with rocky fortunes over the last decade, though with the tide having now truly turned following Steven Schumacher's appointment in January of last year, it has stood the test of time and we're now seeing a persistently-loyal fanbse rewarded for their efforts.

Only one club in League One recorded a higher average away attendance than Bolton, who averaged just under 2,000 supporters on their travels as Schumacher's side finally returned to the Championship, where their numbers and noise have both strengthened in tandem.

Bolton's home support can be outstanding, and their away standing is not too far behind either.

We're looking at both numbers and noise here, of course, and it's the latter criteria that truly does the lifting for Stockport County.

The Hatters have enjoyed a remarkable ascent up the footballing pyramid in recent seasons and that feel-good factor is palpable and reflected in the way that County fans support their side, proving to be something of a driving force towards aggressive unprecedented promotion pushes in League One.

At face value, the statistics would suggest that Stockport's away following doesn't necessarily pull up any trees, as five clubs recorded a superior average attendance to their 1,342 in 25/26.

However, the noise can be eclipsed by very few at its best, with Stockport fans rarely failing to create an almighty racket with the sort of volume, passion and intensity that speaks far louder than the numbers alone.

Another fanbase to have brought bodies and noise decibels aplenty to League One terraces last season was Cardiff City, who gained promotion at the very first time of asking with a fanbase that retained all of its volume and passion after returning to the third-tier for the first time in more than 20 years.

Cardiff's average away attendance of 1,716 was bettered by just two clubs, which is made all the impressive when you consider the fact that only a handful of sides throughout the EFL have to travel further than the Bluebirds.

Indeed, barring vociferous local derbies against Swansea and Bristol City, the Welsh outfit's closest Championship trip this season will be to Birmingham City - yet they regularly record stronger away averages than most while bringing even better noise and relish the 'us against them' mentality that comes with journeys across the border to England, which always carry an extra edge.

Derby County's home atmosphere is even better than what they conjure up on the road, though that's not to say that the Pride Park faithful fail to represent one of the EFL's stronger away fanbases.

In a season that saw John Eustace's side narrowly miss out on a play-off finish, the Rams' average away attendance comfortably exceeded the 2,000 figure and was among the best in the Championship.

Dismal form in the opening months of the current campaign has, quite naturally, reduced the volume of the Rams' ever-loyal travelling contingent, who are admittedly aided by a handy East Midlands location smack-bang in the centre of the country but have historically provided a level of away support bettered by few.

Bradford City's loud and proud fanbase has offered major fuel behind the club's rise from mid-table mediocrity in League Two to a now-consistent status as League One promotion contenders, having made the play-offs during their first season back at third-tier level last time out.

As the Bantams roared on to upset the odds and finish in fourth before losing to Bolton in the semi-finals, no team averaged a higher away attendance than City's 2,000+ figure.

West Yorkshire isn't exactly the easiest location to travel from for many fixtures down south either, even if Bradford were helped by a high volume of relatively-local northern encounters.

Either way, Bradford's home support gets immense credit and their fanbase, in terms of both noise and numbers, deserves just as much for what they get up to away from Valley Parade.

One of the strongest EFL fanbases full-stop comes in the form of Portsmouth, who, akin to many on this list, have stuck with their side through thick and thin before earning some relative rewards after persevering with no shortage of adversity.

John Mousinho's men are now establishing themselves as a second-tier staple once more, and even if Pompey aren't always making a splash on the pitch, you can be sure that they'll catch the eye - and the eardrums - away from it in the terraces.

Fratton Park is a well-documented cauldron of noise, but the same can be said for just about any away end that Portsmouth fans find themselves in.

Those same fans also have to contend with some of the most challenging travel requirements, with their closest trips after local foes Southampton arriving more than 80 miles away in London, yet that never prevents Pompey from creating serious noise on a consistent basis and travelling well after averaging more than 2,000 supporters on the road last time out.

The pride of travelling with both noise and body volume despite being so inconveniently located for just about any away fixture is a glory belonging to Plymouth Argyle, whose fanbase is one of the loudest, proudest and, in many ways, admirable, in all of the land.

It's remarkable that the Pilgrims feature so high when their closest away fixture in the 2026/27 term will be to Reading some 181 miles away following the relegation of rivals Exeter City to League Two, but the fact they still averaged away attendances comfortably in excess of the 1,000 benchmark while always managing to usurp their numbers with noise is testament to an especially-impressive Green Army contingent.

No team has to trek further on their travels, but Plymouth have always shown that it won't stop them.

#2178. What teams AI thinks will be in the EFL Championship in the 2050/51 season

It's always fun to predict how things will look in 20, 50 or even 100 years time, but how will the EFL tables look in 2050?

The Championship is ever-changing. The likes of Lincoln City and Wrexham have made their returns in recent years after decades away, while certain established Premier League clubs are always threatened with dropping into the second tier, too.

Predicting how things will look in the 2050/51 campaign, or in 24 seasons, is almost impossible. The second tier in the 2002/03 season saw Portsmouth win the title and be promoted alongside Leicester City and Wolves, but the likes of Gillingham, Walsall and Grimsby Town were all alongside them in the division.

So, which clubs does AI believe will be in the Championship come 2050? FLW has consulted ChatGPT to find out.

In an ideal world, Birmingham City would be in the Champions League, rather than the Championship, in the future, given the ambition of owner Tom Wagner and the amount of investment put into the Blues side in recent years.

That ownership and investment may not be there in 24 years, though, which could lead to this project crashing and burning.

By 2025, Birmingham will be more than settled in their new 62,000-capacity 'powerhouse stadium', but AI feels that it will be hosting second-tier football.

Blackburn Rovers are one of the longer-serving Championship clubs right now, with this their ninth successive campaign since they were promoted out of League One.

Recent years have seen them bounce between relegation battles and play-off pushes, and under Tony Mowbray, they look to be pretty steady. AI feels that they'll level out back in the second tier come 2050.

Bolton Wanderers' seven-year exile from the Championship came to an end this season, with their long-awaited promotion from League One serving as the final stage of their fightback from near liquidation back in 2019.

The passionate Trotters fanbase will be hoping that the coming years will see them become an established second-tier outfit with the prospect of making a return to the Premier League, and perhaps they will do that in the next couple of decades.

But by 2050/51, AI feels that Bolton will once again be a Championship side.

The first non-current Championship side in the list is Bradford City. The Bantams haven't been a second-tier side in over two decades, but AI feels that they will be in the next 24 years.

Many felt that the West Yorkshire outfit could have gotten into the Championship next season, and they still could, but the departure of Graham Alexander has definitely wounded them, and new boss Michael Duff still has a lot of work to do to get fans onside.

But this is a well-supported club on the rise, and even if it isn't this season, that promotion from League One doesn't seem too far away.

Bristol City being a Championship club at any point feels inevitable. This year marks 18 of the last 20 seasons spent at this level, so perhaps 24 years on from this term, they'll still be finishing 12th in the second tier.

The Robins are at the start of a project led by Michael Skubala, off the back of a summer with some decent investment in promising players across the field, most of whom have come from League One.

If all goes well, perhaps Bristol City could exceed this expectation and be a well-run Premier League side?

Cardiff City haven't historically been a side famed for sticking around in one division. Since the 1974/75 season, the longest stint they've had in one league was a ten-year one in the Championship before their promotion in 2012/13.

Their last second-tier run lasted just six years before relegation in 2024/25, and they answered that with promotion back at the first time of asking.

With Brian Barry-Murphy at the helm, the focus right now is on going back up again, but there'll be no doubt there will be a different direction and another man at the helm come 2050.

Bluebirds fans hope that they'll be able to take on what they hope is a Premier League job after BBM leaves, but AI sees them back in the second tier by 2050.

Charlton Athletic are in a bit of a sticky situation in the Championship right now, failing to win any of their last 11 games and losing four straight. Nathan Jones is praying that Burnley don't get any better anytime soon, else they risk falling into the bottom three.

24 seasons is a long time. Perhaps there's a drop back into League One on the horizon for the Addicks, but ChatGPT at least believes they'll get over that hump and get back into the second tier.

Derby County are another side in real peril at this moment in time. They're also a team that has become synonymous with the Championship over the past couple of decades.

Since being relegated from the Premier League in 2002, 24 years ago, they've spent one year back in the top flight, two in League One, and 21 in the second tier. Given the Rams have been a play-off side in quite a few of those seasons, too, it's quite an achievement for them not to have gone up more than once.

So, in the coming 24 years, it makes sense to put Derby in amongst this Championship lineup.

The second non-current Championship side in the 2050/51 lineup is a club many expect to be a second-tier outfit in 2027/28.

Huddersfield Town have enjoyed a brilliant start to life under Martin Drury, dominating both the attacking and defensive metrics. They have a duo in Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes who have 25 goal involvements between them, and they sit atop League One, looking less and less likely to relinquish that position anytime soon.

With ambitious owner Kevin Nagle overseeing things, he'll be hoping to be a Premier League regular by the time he's ready to relinquish control. By 2050, though, AI feels that the Terriers will be back in the second tier.

Both Bradford and Huddersfield will be joined by West Yorkshire rivals and the first current Premier League side on the list, Leeds United, which will make for some tasty matchups over the year for sure.

The Whites put in a brilliant showing in the second half of last season to retain their top-flight status, and after starting this year on the front foot, some Leeds fans are expressing some frustration at the number of draws their side are seemingly settling for.

Again, 24 years is a long time, so perhaps Daniel Farke can turn things around again and bring the Yorkshire giants back to being European contenders. But the German won't be in charge come 2050, and ChatGPT believes that they'll have slid back into the Championship by then.

#2177. How Dave Challinor has reacted to shock Sheffield Wednesday loss to Oldham

Dave Challinor’s reaction to Sheffield Wednesday’s FA Cup defeat to Oldham Athletic has received a big reaction from supporters.

The new Owls boss oversaw his first game in charge on Sunday, with the team suffering defeat away to the League Two side.

Calum Kavanagh put the Latics ahead in the 66th minute, but Davis Keillor-Dunn responded to bring the game to extra-time.

But Will Sutton’s strike in the second half of the extended period gave the hosts a 2-1 advantage that Challinor’s side were unable to overcome.

The Yorkshire outfit have been eliminated from the FA Cup in the first round, highlighting the size of the task at hand for the new head coach.

The League One side will be aiming to compete for promotion back to the Championship this season, having brought in the former Stockport County boss in place of Henrik Pedersen.

Challinor has expressed his disappointment at the performance from his Sheffield Wednesday side, even though he knew that there was never going to be immediate progress after just a few days in charge.

He criticised the first half performance for being too passive, before praising the improvement in the second half, despite ultimately conceding two goals to suffer defeat.

“Really disappointed,” said Challinor, via the club’s official X account.

Could Josh Windass return to Sheffield Wednesday when his Wrexham contract expires in 2028?

“It was always going to be the case, it was never going to be linear in terms of what progress looks like.

“Probably knew things coming into the game, and coming into the club, and that’s reinforced those things, and the things that need to change.

“We’re in a position, we’re a little bit hamstrung in terms of the team we can pick, and who can play certain minutes, and all those types of things, which is almost like pre-season, not middle of November in the middle of a League One season.

“First half, miles too passive, like a testimonial.

Is Dave Challinor the man to bring Sheffield Wednesday forward? Comment your opinion below

“And players maybe being a little bit protective because of what the back end of the game looks like.

“Second half, much, much better, having our best spell and obviously concede two really poor goals, but that’s nothing to take away from Oldham, who deservedly go through.”

Challinor highlighted a particular issue with fitness within the squad, suggesting that standards have to improve if players are going to reach the goals they’ve set out for their careers.

“Great reaction to that, and we’re on the front foot, and like I say there will be pleasing stuff from the second half,” he continued.

“The extra time period, you know what it’s like, it can go either way.

“Physically, we’ve got to be miles better.

“You look at, I’ll use Barry [Bannan] as an example, but he’s 36-years-old and he’s running around all over the place, and we’ve got players that will be aspirational in terms of where they want to go and play that are getting cramps left, right and centre.

“Dish has probably got a good excuse for that, he’s not played, but the rest, if we want to play like what we all agree a Sheffield Wednesday team should look like, and be front-foot, we need to have those behaviours every single day.

“In order when we come out here and play, the supporters see and we represent them in a better form than what we did tonight.”

Sheffield Wednesday are now winless in their last five games in all competitions, with their last victory coming against AFC Wimbledon on 17 October.

Sheffield Wednesday fans have backed Challinor’s assessment of the game and the squad’s fitness issues.

Supporters are behind the new manager, suggesting that they think he’s surprised at the fitness levels of the players.

Fans are optimistic that the 51-year-old is going to raise standards, believing that the players have had it easy for far too long.

The supporters are also pleased to see that the new manager is giving an honest assessment of the game, instead of offering empty platitudes.

Many are hopeful that Challinor will now work on improving the overall fitness level of the squad, with some wondering if the issue has caused the injury problems of the recent past.

Fans are willing to give the former Stockport boss time to turn things around, claiming that it will be a slow process to fix the problems with the team.

Supporters believe that Challinor knows what he’s talking about, and are encouraged by his angry reaction to the loss.

Next up for the Owls in the league is a home clash against Plymouth Argyle on 14 November in a 3pm kick-off.

The defeat to Oldham has revealed to Challinor the size of the task at hand, and he knows it won’t be a quick process in turning things around.

Sheffield Wednesday reached a significant low point last season, and it was always naive to think that it could all be undone in just one year.

But Challinor is an exciting appointment because he knows what it takes to compete to a high standard at this level, and he can reintroduce that to the club after a challenging year in which the Owls came out of administration.

Despite the loss, fans seem optimistic about the future under the new manager, and these comments have backed that belief.

#2175. Inglorious Hearts crash as flying Falkirk dismantle Wouter Vrancken's toiling Jambos

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the William Hill Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Read more: Furious Aberdeen fans demand Stephen Robinson axe amid miserable form

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#2174. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

Today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the new players, to build our team to get their best today.

I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

She wore… she wore… she wore a yellow ribbon …

Two changes – Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson make debuts. Joao Gomes misses the match as the first of his three-game suspension and Marco Bizot drops to the bench.

Double debuts 🤩Your Villa XI to face Arsenal this evening 👋 pic.twitter.com/Zue0ZTSJt9

Arteta names unchanged starting XI but Bruno Guimaraes is fit for the bench. Ezri Konsa joins him there.

In its rightful place 🏠🏆 pic.twitter.com/FMH4zve1aD

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#2173. Todd Cantwell reacts as Blackburn Rovers fire West Ham, Scott Parker dig

Scott Parker is already making headlines for all the wrong reasons in charge of West Ham, with the ex-England international having endured a challenging start to proceedings at the London Stadium by failing to win any of his opening two games - and it's causing reaction from both Hammers supporters and opposition players alike.

West Ham only parted company with Nuno Espirito Santo less than a week ago in the wake of successive home defeats against two promotion rivals in West Bromwich Albion and Southampton, which saw the Championship outfit swiftly relieve the long-under-fire Portuguese boss of his duties in favour of sealing a return for Parker.

The 46-year-old had been out of work since leaving Burnley towards the end of the previous campaign, but has wasted no time in getting his feet back under the table and experienced an action-packed debut in the Hammers dugout by claiming a 3-3 draw at Cardiff City last Wednesday after his side had stunningly fallen to a three-goal defecit before the break in South Wales.

West Ham were hot favourites heading into Saturday afternoon's second consecutive away encounter against Blackburn Rovers, although Parker's men would once again flatter to deceive and went two goals down courtesy of strikes from Andri Gudjohnsen and ex-Hammers winger Dapo Afolayan before Joel Piroe's late finish halved the scoreline without setting up yet another dramatic comeback on the road.

Parker's cagey post-match interview at Ewood Park has sparked quite the reaction, too, and after Clarets supporters pointed out just how fatigued and frustrated the former Fulham and Bournemouth boss appeared so early in his return to the club, Blackburn have taken something different from his comments.

Ewood Park isn't exactly renowned for providing an intense and aggressive atmosphere, though Blackburn did not need anything extra to get over the line at home to the pre-season title favourites in what will be remembered as a memorable victory against the odds for Tony Mowbray's side.

That didn't stop Parker from aiming a clear dig towards the East Lancashire outfit, though, remarking in his interview how, on the coach journey to Ewood Park, he "didn't see a Blackburn fan".

Blackburn, however, have been very quick to remind the ex-Burnley figure - hardly a popular presence in this corner of Lancashire in any case, of course - that there were indeed fans present to see his side's winless run continue with a cheeky dig.

The club posted a clip of his quote in a video uploaded to Instagram featuring footage of the Rovers home crowd buoyantly celebrating the hosts' two goals, which was accompanied by a provocative caption reading: "Found some for ya, Scott 😉."

FLW's West Ham fan pundit believes the Hammers should look to offload goalkeeper Mads Hermansen in the January transfer window.

Blackburn are certainly having the last laugh right now and that wasn't limited to the social media admins, with supporters joining the pile-on and some players even getting involved in the antics for good measure.

Namely, club captain Todd Cantwell earned the right to poke fun at the Hammers after enjoying a standout individual display against Parker's side, and the talented playmaker kept it short and sweet by commenting "😂."

His one-emoji dig was followed up by Sam Morsy, who was also in stitches and commented 🤣🤣👏."

Cantwell's comment, unlike that from Morsy, appeared to ignite reaction as some West Ham fans responded to the divisive ex-Norwich City and Rangers starlet, yet he's likely to simply sit back and laugh as his side continue upsetting the odds while ruffling a few feathers in the process.

Blackburn's swipe at Parker was shared via X alongside Instagram, where it gathered an interesting and mixed reaction from both sets of supporters.

West Ham fans, for example, were naturally unimpressed, and this one punter quipped how Rovers' footage failed to capture the high volume of empty seats that we invariably see at Ewood Park.

This fan, meanwhile, is not keen on just how much Blackburn have posted about the victory, suggesting that West Ham's trip up north represented a "cup final" occasion for their more modest Championship counterparts.

Another Hammer banged the drum for humility among those at Ewood, claiming that Parker's quotes had been taken out of context in an effort to gain a cheeky one-up in less-than-humble fashion.

Blackburn fans, by contrast, have been lapping it all up - and who can blame them?

Before the season started, Rovers were widely tipped for relegation whereas Saturday's visitors, fresh off the back of 14 successive seasons in the Premier League with heavy spending prior to an unprecedented relegation last time out, have been backed by the masses to complete a swift top-flight return.

It's not exactly going to plan, though, and Blackburn supporters didn't hold back after their club's jibe, which was described as "unbelievable content" by one fan.

Another was equally happy to have a laugh at Parker's expense, and that can only come as little surprise in light of the manager's aforementioned unpopularity among the Blackburn faithful following his previous exploits with bitter rivals Burnley.

Some have been even more cynical towards Parker, though, and this Blackburn fan labelled the ex-Clarets promotion-winner as "the most annoying manager for about six years now" ahead of cited polarising figures such as Leicester City's Russell Martin and Nathan Jones of Charlton Athletic.

The 7,000-strong West Ham contingent that travelled up to Ewood Park on Saturday returned down south with yet more disappointment as Parker fell short of clinching his first set of three points for the second occasion in under a week.

It's nowhere near good enough for a side with designs on lifting the title with numerous Premier League-quality performers to call upon and, in the last week, the stewardship of a manager who enjoyed a strong playing career with the club before achieving three second-tier promotions in charge of just as many clubs, and he'll be shaking off the jibes and jokes to go back to the drawing board and assess precisely what went wrong.

The encounter itself saw Blackburn score two of their three shots on target, which is hardly a ringing endorsement for goalkeeper Mads Hermansen amid ever-intensifying supporter scrutiny towards the Dane.

West Ham, by contrast, would manage only five shots on target from 21 in total, but with the likes of Jarrod Bowen, Mohamadou Kante and goalscorer Piroe all spurning some glorious opportunities as their side dominated both the possession and chance-creating stakes, the hapless Hammers will scarcely believe their luck riding some of it to overturn a three-goal blitz at Cardiff days earlier.

The two results are hardly representative of an outfit capable of arresting the slide, making up ground and eventually finishing in the top-two, though, and having now fallen out of the play-offs entirely heading into this month's upcoming international break, Parker will need to get it right sooner rather than later at the London Stadium.

Blackburn Rovers and West Ham fans, how do you feel about the dig towards Scott Parker? Who will be having the last laugh at the end of the season? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

As for Blackburn, they won't mind one bit and are contrastingly over-performing on their own expectations after returning to winning ways in emphatic fashion against one of the strongest and most well-backed sides they will face all season.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Dave Challinor's debut as Sheffield Wednesday manager didn't go to plan, as the Owls were dumped out of the FA Cup by League Two opposition in Oldham Athletic, and there were parts of the performance he was especially angered by.

Oldham were good value for their win after extra time, with Wednesday putting in a tired performance that not many were expecting from Challinor's first game in charge. It's the first time that the 51-year-old has opened up a dugout role without a win.

The first half, especially, wasn't good enough by the new manager's standards. Wednesday dominated possession, but only had one shot and just three touches in the Latics' box. It was quite reminiscent of what angered Owls fans about Henrik Pedersen's setup.

Challinor wasn't going to let this become the norm, though, and was seen writing plenty of notes in his notebook for what was going to be quite the angry team talk at the break.

After the game, Challinor continued to cut a frustrated figure, with the majority of fans agreeing with what he was saying, with the overarching feeling that some of the players aren't where they should be physically at this stage in the campaign.

Most Wednesday supporters felt disappointed with how Pedersen would protect players after poor results, whereas the new boss seems content with outlining where things aren't good enough, which in turn is winning fans over.

While it would have been an ideal scenario for Dave Challinor to walk in, tweak one or two things and Wednesday go from strength to strength, the first 45 minutes of his tenure in charge highlight that this definitely won't be the case.

Challinor is coming into a side that, by his own admission, isn't there physically and is struggling massively with injury.

Mason Burstow is the latest casualty, while Ashley Maynard-Brewer was forced off during the game and Harry Gray was removed from the squad at the last minute after failing to get through the warm-up.

#2171. Kim Hellberg footage after Middlesbrough's draw v Watford is becoming a talking point

Middlesbrough dropped points and failed to score for the second time this week on Saturday at Watford, and Boro boss Kim Hellberg was seen visibly frustrated after the final whistle.

The draw at Vicarage Road saw Middlesbrough relinquish the top spot in the Championship ahead of the November international break, with Birmingham City climbing above them on goal difference.

It's not how Boro would have wanted to sign off this mini block of fixtures between international breaks, and the performance against Watford, especially, would have provided plenty of food for thought in the dugout.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

Indeed, this was the second successive game without leading talisman and Championship top scorer Will Lankshear due to injury, and it's almost universally agreed that if the 21-year-old was leading the line on Saturday, they'd have cruised to victory, as Boro had 18 shots, 34 touches in Watford's box and four big chances, but couldn't score.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg has shown how passionate he is about the game in the 12 months he's spent in charge at the Riverside. Therefore, it was clear that a result like this, following such a dominant performance, was going to affect him.

After the game, the Swede was filmed staring blankly at the ground for around half a minute, just reflecting on the game, and Boro fans have reacted accordingly.

Some have made jokey comments about the state of the frontline when Lankshear is injured. One Boro fan took it upon themselves to caption the video, "What having Kyle Joseph as an attacking option does to man." Another commented, "Please god make Will be fit, please god make Will be fit…..🙏."

"He’s got Kyle Joseph depression," was also among the reactions to the video.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

The majority of comments in response to Hellberg's post-match reaction were about how invested he is in the game, though, and Middlesbrough fans know how lucky they are to have the Swede in charge.

"You can just tell this isn’t performative. Like the fist bumps and the celebrations when we win, or the tears during the play-off debacle last season, Kim ‘gets it’, he’s immersed himself into the #Boro way. Never seen a manager so invested in us," one Boro fan tweeted.

"Carries it all, the highs and lows just like the fans. “A good leader leads the people from above them. A great leader leads the people from within them," was also among the comments, as was, "The reaction of a man who puts the weight of the world on his own shoulders #UTB."

"Very powerful, but also makes me want to give him a hug and tell him he's one of my favourite ever Boro gaffers and everything will be alright," someone commented in response to the video, showcasing the love and respect Boro fans have towards their head coach.

This is the reaction of a man spent after a disappointing result, having coached what was effectively the perfect game.

Plenty of head coaches nowadays are focused on the journey, the performance levels and good underlying numbers, and Hellberg is definitely one of those, but he also recognises how important it is to win games, too.

As one Boro fan mentioned, he carries the weight of expectation amongst Middlesbrough fans, who are desperate to return to the Premier League after a decade away, and you can imagine he takes not winning as seriously as some of those in the stands do, too.

It's reactions like this that are why many are touting Hellberg to become a top-flight manager in the near future, and Boro supporters hope it'll be with them.

However, it's hard to ignore the fact that, while Lankshear sits on the sidelines, Middlesbrough struggles to score goals and win games.

Boro's wasteful nature in front of goal dominated the narrative surrounding them in the final few months of last season as they slipped out of the running for automatic promotion and into the play-offs, and they could have been out of sight in the first half of their play-off semi-final first leg against Southampton if not for poor finishing, too.

Lankshear has papered over those cracks, as he's been brilliant at finishing the plenty of chances Middlesbrough create in a game, but the alarm bells are starting to ring without him.

Do you think Middlesbrough can turn their finishing troubles around without Will Lankshear in the side? Let us know in the comments.

Hopefully, the 21-year-old will be back after the international break and won't suffer any more injury setbacks, as that could be the difference between promotion and some grim de ja vu.

It's something Hellberg will be mulling over for the next two weeks, and it seemingly started immediately after the final whistle at Watford.

A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2169. West Ham face Taty Castellanos, River Plate transfer exit threat

As West Ham continue to fall short of rekindling their fortunes despite Scott Parker's recent appointment, the possibility of Taty Castellanos departing the London Stadium in the coming months has now emerged in a development that will spark mixed reactions from Hammers supporters.

West Ham's return to the Championship following 14 successive seasons of solid Premier League standing is not going to plan right now, with the East Londoners appearing increasingly unlikely to seal a previously-expected top-flight return at the very first time of asking as champions.

A mixed run of form featuring consecutive home defeats at home to a pair of promotion rivals in Southampton and West Bromwich Albion ultimately ended Nuno Espirito Santo's unpopular tenure in charge, and the Portuguese boss has been swiftly succeeded by former Hammers midfielder Parker.

The ex-Bournemouth and Fulham boss, having already achieved three promotions from the second-tier with as many clubs after most recently guiding Burnley back to the promised land in 2025 before his dismissal towards the end of the previous campaign, has encountered a challenging return to the club thus far, though, taking just one point from his opening two matches.

Last Wednesday's thrilling 3-3 comeback draw at Cardiff City after overturning a three-goal defecit at half-time was followed up by a disappointing 2-1 defeat away to Blackburn Rovers over the weekend, and with the Hammers yet to enjoy the anticipated upturn under Parker, they now face the threat of losing one of their big-name performers once the January window rolls around.

Castellanos has endured a particularly difficult and underwhelming introduction to the Championship, which the Argentine forward was expected to light up after his mid-season arrival back in January preceded encouraging goalscoring form in spite of his side's ultimate failure to dodge the drop.

Six goals from 18 Premier League appearances means that the current return of just one strike across 14 second-tier fixtures - nine of which have been starts - is not what fans were anticipating, and they had presented vocal criticism towards the divisive 28-year-old for a number of weeks before Parker hauled the attacker off at the interval against the Bluebirds and then dropped his name out of the starting line-up at Ewood Park.

It has now emerged that Castellanos could leave East London as early as January, with a fresh report from Argentine-based outlet El Intransigente claiming strong long-term interest from River Plate.

As per the update, River Plate have held interest in the two-cap Argentine international's services in recent windows and he represents a "top target" in the eyes of manager Leonardo Ponzio.

Blackburn Rovers captain Todd Cantwell has been among those reacting to the club's dig towards Scott Parker's West Ham after Saturday's 2-1 victory

It's said that the Buenos Aries-based giants feel strongly about Castellano's profile and international experience, with the striker having risen to prominence outside of his native Argentina in Uruguay with Montevideo City Torque before enjoying productive spells at New York City, Girona and Lazio ahead of joining West Ham earlier this year for a reported £26 million figure on a four-and-a-half year contract.

West Ham supporters have grown increasingly critical of Castellanos and his long-term future under Parker remains unclear at this moment in time, although a fresh hurdle could prevent River Plate from sealing the deal.

River Plate have been presented with a significant obstacle to overcome if they intend on returning Castellanos to his homeland, as it's a move which wouldn't come cheaply for the 38-time Primera Division champions.

Indeed, the report has added that the salary Castellanos earns at the London Stadium is the main challenge for River Plate right now, leaving the club to weigh up alternative options such as acquiring the sought-after frontman on loan or even purchasing a percentage of his rights.

Both of those options, of course, would require the prior approval of West Ham, whose own stance on potentially parting ways with the ex-Lazio striker just a year after his arrival with a club likely unable to recoup the figure of purchase is also not yet known.

It's noted that Castellanos' lengthy contract with the Championship promotion hopefuls puts Parker's side in a comfortable negotiating decision, and hold all the cards as River Plate will not be able to wrap up any deal without their support.

Interestingly, however, the update also makes reference to previous interest elsewhere, reminding that Castellanos had reportedly wished to leave West Ham in the summer amid loan interest from Seville-based rivals Real Betis and Sevilla that never materialised.

The London Stadium faithful remain very much divided on Castellanos at the moment, with some making their minds up on the out-of-form forward and others willing to persist with further patience.

Prior claims of a January exit if the price is met at the end of the previous month saw some West Ham fans refuse to hold back on their feelings about Castellanos' future, and this one fan believes that his hapless form in the Championship would make for no great loss if he was to depart.

Another would be happy to see the Hammers striker leave at any cost, even if the club themselves surely won't take that stance.

Castellanos has left some frustrated for reasons beyond his inability to find the back of the net on a regular basis, too, and having formerly scored at a relatively-prolific rate leading the line for a side relegated from the Premier League, his work-rate and application have been called into question.

His display in the aforementioned draw at Cardiff drew particular criticism, and West Ham were a much more fluid, functional and threatening outfit once the Argentine was withdrawn for Joel Piroe at the break.

Now, with the Suriname international scoring in successive encounters, it's unclear how Castellanos will force his way back into starting contention ahead of a positional rival with a historically-goal-laden hit-rate at this level.

West Ham fans, how do you feel about Taty Castellanos' future? Would you hold onto the striker, or is it time to cash in? What should his valuation be? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

But there are other fans who continue to stand by Castellanos, and considering how he fared at the highest level last time out, it's no great surprise that certain supporters still believe he can come good in the second-tier.

Either way, there are plenty of West Ham fans who, despite the criticism of the majority, do feel that the divisive striker would thrive in a system that emphasises chance creation under a manager willing to trust in his services and get the best out of an undeniably-talented striker with pedigree in more prestigious and higher-quality divisions.

This punter, meanwhile, reckons that cashing in on Castellanos would be a "stupid decision", but only time will tell to see what action West Ham decide to take and whether a deal can successfully be thrashed out with River Plate.

#2168. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Harry Maguire-5.5            Was decent in the first half but wasn’t much of an answer to Tottenham going forward in the second half

Lisandro Martinez-5      Took his eyes off the ball, resulting in conceding a late goal off Solanke.

Luke Shaw-6      Went up high on the pitch and remained a threat with his overlapping threat. Was involved in the scuffle that got Bentancur a red card for headbutting.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

Carlos Baleba (58’)-6.5  A decent debut overall for the Cameroon international. He put in a couple of dangerous balls up the field, including a clear ball to Mbeumo on a counter, who was denied by Kinsky.

Diogo Dalot (58’)-6      Provided a decent attacking threat when brought on around the hour mark.

Joshua Zirkzee (58’)-6   Showed plenty of promise and was a threat after he was brought in around the hour mark.
